entry.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Generative Recommendation
entry.summary: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the cold-start problem of recommending creators a user does not yet follow, arguing that the Semantic ID layer used in generative recommenders, not the language model, is the main bottleneck. The authors propose Atomic Creator Token (ACT), which gives each creator its own vocabulary token trained end-to-end, avoiding SID collisions and blocked gradients. In a controlled comparison on production data, ACT outperforms a matched SID baseline on creator-level Recall@15, and it also leads on the public KuaiRand dataset. A live A/B test shows directionally positive results on every reported metric. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose per-creator atomic tokens trained end-to-end, comparing against semantic IDs on production data and KuaiRand, plus a live A/B test.

entry.title: SCRAMJet: An Ultra-Low-Latency Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger
entry.summary: SCRAMJet: An Ultra Low Latency JetClass-Scale Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger arXiv · Oct 21, 2026This paper presents SCRAMJet, a transformer encoder for Level-1 triggers at the High-Luminosity LHC that replaces multi-head attention with a low-rank projection and uses per-parameter learned fixed-point quantization. It is compiled to Verilog for FPGA implementation and is evaluated on the ten-class JetClass dataset, where it meets timing on a Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P at 147 ns. The authors also report that resource-aware training can silently remove attention channels from the compiled circuit, and that a floor on the attention datalane prevents this. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces multi-head attention with low-rank projection plus learned quantization and Verilog compilation; the authors report JetClass results and a virtual-channel effect.

entry.title: Faces or Models? Where Age Gaps in Expression Recognition Come From
entry.summary: Faces or Models? Where the Age Gap in Facial Expression Recognition Comes From arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This study tested five open-source facial expression recognition models on the FACES database, which contains 2,052 posed photos of 171 adults aged 19 to 80. Every model was less accurate on older faces, by 11.7 to 15.2 percentage points, and human raters also performed worse on them. Retraining only the final classification layer on older faces shrank the gap to 4 points or less, suggesting the models' features can represent older faces and the problem lies in how the final layer was trained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate facial aging from model training, comparing five FER models with human and geometry baselines on 2,052 photos, reporting the gap shrinks after refitting only the final layer.

entry.title: Think in 360°: Benchmarking and training AI to reason over panoramic video
entry.summary: Think in 360deg: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces PanoVideoBench, a manually annotated benchmark of 1,000 questions for understanding panoramic video across all viewing directions and time. It also builds PanoVideoCoT, a reasoning dataset of 13,465 QA pairs grounded in real panoramic video. The resulting model, PanoVideoReasoner, reaches 55.7% on the benchmark, improving its backbone and the previous state of the art.

entry.title: Observable-specific validity tests for scientific AI: controlled approximations and intervention response
entry.summary: Observable-Specific Validity Tests for Scientific AI: Controlled Approximations and Intervention Response arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes observable-specific validity records for scientific AI that link a simplified model to its reference model, error measure, tolerance, parameter domain, and transformations or interventions. It gives explicit displacement and velocity certificates for a singularly perturbed oscillator and uses exact Hubbard dimer relations to show how energy and response criteria accept different coupling domains. In 16 repeated neural fits, imposing dimensional homogeneity reduced energy scale transfer error from 52.3% to 0.0768% and raised the median fraction satisfying both gap and response tolerances from zero to 100%.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling
entry.summary: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper presents ArchOR, an archetype-centric skill agent that extends OptSkills with two retrieval modules: Centroid-Aware Representation Learning (CARL) and Signature-Guided Retrieval (S³R). Candidates are ranked by weighted Jaccard overlap of structural signatures, and an arbitration rule decides when the structural route replaces the original selector. Using the same DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone, ArchOR reaches 65.00% Micro-Avg. Pass@1 across five benchmarks, improving over OptSkills.

entry.title: Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes): a minimalist way to widen the residual stream separately from layer compute
entry.summary: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes), which widens the residual state of a Transformer while keeping per-layer compute width fixed. Layers are grouped into blocks, with standard PreNorm layers inside each block and a wider PostNorm outer residual connecting blocks, bridged by learned read/write projections. The authors report that HiRes beats vanilla residual addition across model sizes and depths, with fitted scaling laws indicating a 1.30-fold FLOPs efficiency gain. On OLMoE-1B-7B pretraining for 500B tokens, it reports 0.0208 lower training loss and 1.14 points higher downstream accuracy.

entry.title: NormDetect: Low-false-positive detection of machine-generated web text
entry.summary: NormDetect: Anchored Calibration for Low-False-Positive Detection of Machine-Generated Web Text arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents NormDetect, a method for spotting text written by large language models on web platforms while keeping false flags on human writing very low. It anchors a learned per-section head to the normalized zero-shot score and calibrates the threshold on human text only. On eight RAID benchmark sections with eleven attacks, it raises recall at 0.1% calibrated false positive rate by 5.0 points over normalized Binoculars, with human false positive rate kept at most 1% in every section.

entry.title: BlindToChange: Do AI Agents Check for Recent Changes When They Need To, Not Just When Asked?
entry.summary: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces BlindToChange, a benchmark testing whether AI agents proactively discover recent real-world events that affect their recommendations. Requests state only the final information need without naming the event, which is drawn automatically from Wikidata. Agents perform much worse when the event is not mentioned than when asked directly, and most failures occur because agents do not search to verify whether a relevant fact has changed.

entry.title: What we keep when we forget: how replacement methods shape pruned MoE experts
entry.summary: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper compares replacement operators for training-free pruning of Mixture-of-Experts expert layers across several models, including OLMoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Moonlight. It finds that how the surviving experts' gate scale is handled has the largest effect, with renormalizing survivors' gates on routers trained without top-k renormalization costing 0.8 to 8.5 points. The authors introduce a low-rank "tilted novice" map that improves on MoNE's constant replacement at 50% pruning.

entry.title: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer
entry.summary: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether auxiliary trajectory preferences help small language models improve themselves and transfer skills under limited supervision. It compares a confidence-based metric (SC) with an entropy-based metric (UID-Conj.) used for online reward augmentation and offline training on correct responses. UID-Conj. shows gains over unmodified TTRL online and over uniform weighting in offline weighted SFT, though the benefits vary by task.

entry.title: Counterfactual pair augmentation to improve small pointwise LLM judges
entry.summary: Counterfactual Pairwise Augmentation Improves Small Pointwise LLM Judges arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CPA (Counterfactual Pairwise Augmentation), a method for training small language models that score a single response against a criterion. For each pointwise item, CPA synthesizes and audits a counterfactual response to the same query with the opposite label, then fine-tunes the judge jointly on pointwise and pairwise data while deploying only in pointwise mode. In experiments on six binary criteria with Qwen3-8B LoRA adapters, CPA outperforms pointwise-only training and model merging, and surpasses the zero-shot frontier judge Gemini 3.6 Flash.

entry.title: One verdict is not enough: regression testing for learned world models and their test harnesses
entry.summary: One Verdict Is Not Enough: Regression Testing Learned World Models and Their Test Harnesses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents TetraState, a regression-testing protocol for paired possible/impossible video tests. Each test runs under four fixed model-native configurations, and its number of correct verdicts assigns it to one of four outcome classes. On all 506 IntPhys 2 Main tests, two V-JEPA 2 harness revisions change modal accuracy by only 0.2 and 2.6 points but change 11 and 214 test labels, with 43 regressions that keep the modal verdict and so escape a modal-verdict flip check.

entry.title: MUON-RT: A Momentum-Free Muon Optimizer Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for LLM Self-Distillation
entry.summary: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes Muon-RT, which reuses the displacement between teacher and student models in self-distillation to replace momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices, reducing persistent training memory. With SDFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less memory. With SDPO on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.

entry.title: Learning dynamics by matching velocities: a simulation-free training method for nonlinear systems
entry.summary: Learning to evolve by matching velocities arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to learn the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems. The authors propose Velocity Matching (VM), a training objective that avoids simulating trajectories and backpropagating through numerical solvers. They develop stability estimates that control trajectory errors through velocity errors. In numerical experiments on nonlinear ODEs and semi-discretized time-dependent PDEs, VM is reported to be more accurate than trajectory-based objectives. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose simulation-free Velocity Matching, with stability and universal approximation theory linking it to A-stable Runge-Kutta schemes; reported gains on ODEs and semi-discretized PDEs.

entry.title: Statistical inference when predictions shape the data they learn from
entry.summary: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies performativity, where prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, as in policy-making and self-evolving AI systems. The authors build an end-to-end statistical inference framework, deriving central limit theorems and covariance recursions for repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent. They propose consistent covariance estimators based on policy perturbations and score matching, and extend prediction-powered inference to this setting. Experiments show that ignoring propagated uncertainty can cause substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend statistical inference to performative repeated risk minimization and gradient descent, deriving covariance recursions and prediction-powered inference, evaluated on synthetic and LL

entry.title: Online fair division of chores with upgrade recourse
entry.summary: Online Fair Division of Chores with Upgrade Recourse arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies online fair division of indivisible chores among n agents, where earlier assignments may be revised but each previously assigned chore must be replaced by a different chore the agent finds no more costly. The authors show that a simple adaptation of round robin achieves envy-freeness up to one chore (EF1) together with a (2-1/n)-approximation of the maximin share (MMS). They also prove that no deterministic algorithm without predictions can do better on this MMS factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a round-robin adaptation achieving EF1 and (2-1/n)-MMS under upgrade recourse, plus a matching deterministic lower bound and prediction-based improvements.

entry.title: VESPER: Learning Free-Energy Landscapes Online with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
entry.summary: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective arXiv · Oct 31, 2026VESPER is a method that learns free-energy landscapes over collective variables while molecular dynamics simulations run. The evolving model biases the simulations to cross energy barriers more easily, and data from several tempering levels train one shared model without reweighting. The authors prove conditional convergence of the coupled dynamics and test the method on alanine dipeptide, alanine tetrapeptide, methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511), and chignolin. ★★★★ Notable: The authors couple enhanced sampling with neural free-energy learning via one convex variational objective over multiple tempering levels, reporting tests on alanine peptides, methane dehydrogenation,

entry.title: Two strategies for drawing conclusions: shaping representations versus reasoning in context
entry.summary: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper formalizes two inference strategies: a geometric strategy that gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect relational structure, making later inference cheap, and an algebraic strategy that flexibly reasons over novel relations given in context at extra computational cost. The authors identify opposing signatures of these strategies in transitive inference. Experiments with humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models demonstrate these effects. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize geometric and algebraic inference and report opposing signatures in transitive inference across humans, trained networks, and LLMs, with causal interventions.

entry.title: Measuring How Well Nonlinear Embeddings Preserve Local and Global Structure
entry.summary: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines how well dimension reduction methods such as t-SNE, UMAP, and PCA preserve local and global data structure. The authors derive a local fidelity score L and a global fidelity score G from one shared locality curve, and propose an LG reversal test to check whether two maps trade off locality and globality and at what scale to switch between them. Across 156 maps of twelve datasets with up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.89 and 0.96. The test confirms the usual claim on seven datasets and finds neighbor embeddings more global on two retail datasets and two rolled-up manifolds. ★★★★ Notable: Unifies local and global fidelity as one curve statistic and proposes an LG reversal test, which the authors validate on 156 maps across twelve datasets.

entry.title: A generative foundation model for brain imaging analysis (BrainGFM)
entry.summary: A generative foundation model for computational brain imaging arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes BrainGFM, a reusable and reconfigurable generative foundation model for computational brain imaging. Pretrained on about 1.3 million MRI and CT slices, it supports task-aligned data synthesis, low-data predictive learning, and image reconstruction. It improved segmentation and classification across 48 downstream tasks and was validated on 4,796 stroke patients from six centers. In a human-AI study, BrainGFM assistance raised radiologists' stroke-subtyping accuracy by 14% in relative terms. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a reusable generative brain-imaging prior, validated across 48 downstream tasks and multicenter stroke cohorts with a human-AI study.

entry.title: Model collapse can be avoided even as real data shrinks, via a sharp criterion for iterative Gaussian estimation.
entry.summary: Model Collapse Is Avoidable Even as Real Data Vanishes: A Sharp Criterion for Iterative Gaussian Estimation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies whether repeatedly training on a mix of real data and a model's own generated samples causes model collapse, focusing on iterative estimation of a multivariate Gaussian's mean and covariance. Each iteration mixes real samples with samples from the previous estimate without distinguishing them. The authors give a single equivalent condition for consistency of the estimators and show collapse is avoided for any fixed positive real-data fraction, or a vanishing fraction that does not vanish too quickly. However, the mean estimator's convergence slows as the real-data fraction approaches zero. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a single equivalent condition for consistency of iterative Gaussian mean and covariance estimation with mixed real and generated data, supported by CIFAR-10 diffusion experiments.

entry.title: OPINE: Orthogonal Projection in Invertible Nonlinear Embeddings for Turbulent Flows
entry.summary: OPINE: Orthogonal Projection in Invertible Nonlinear Embeddings for Turbulent Flows arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces OPINE, a method that learns an invertible nonlinear coordinate transformation and then applies proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) in the transformed coordinates to compress physical fields such as turbulent flows. Because the transformation is invertible, all information loss occurs in the POD projection, so one trained model yields reduced coordinates of every smaller dimension by ordering its basis. The authors prove that their alternating training update converges locally to the exact POD subspace, and they evaluate the method on synthetic manifolds, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and Burgers dynamics, two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow, and three-dimensional minimal channel flow. ★★★★ Notable: Combines an invertible nonlinear map with POD for single-model reduced coordinates; the authors report comparisons against POD and autoencoders on several turbulent datasets.

entry.title: A family of prior forces for implicit denoiser priors and how they guide decisions in linear inverse problems
entry.summary: The Prior-Force Family of Implicit Denoiser Priors and Its Decisions in Linear Inverse Problems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies implicit priors built from Gaussian denoisers, used in methods such as plug-and-play (PnP), regularization by denoising (RED), and score-based approaches. It defines a prior-force family indexed by noise variance so these implicit priors can be compared with explicit ones like MAP priors. The authors compare the resulting energies for MMSE denoisers and conclude that the noise level acts as a prior parameter rather than a step size. Experiments with exact priors support these predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define a prior-force family for Gaussian denoisers and compare PnP, RED and MAP energies, reporting that noise level acts as a prior parameter, with experiments on exact priors.

entry.title: Faithful where you look: anchor-based tests miss invented text in image-to-video generation
entry.summary: Faithful Where You Look: Anchor-Based Evaluation Hides Text Fabrication in Image-Conditioned Video Generation arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper examines whether image-conditioned video models stay faithful to the real places they are shown. Using 48 Tokyo storefront references and four models from three vendors, the authors find that existing text benchmarks check only an annotated sign and miss problems elsewhere. In the surrounding periphery, 36-54% of generated text regions have no counterpart in the reference, versus 1.6% for a control, despite prompts forbidding new readable text. Code, annotations, scores and preregistrations are released. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show anchor-based benchmarks hide text fabrication; they report 36-54% fabricated periphery text across four models and release code and preregistrations.

entry.title: AegisBench: Auditing Drone Person Detection in Disaster Conditions
entry.summary: AegisBench: Auditing Aerial Search-and-Rescue Person Detection Under the Conditions It Is Deployed In arXiv · Oct 17, 2026AegisBench is a benchmark that tests drone-based person detectors under nine physically motivated disaster-related image corruptions applied to the HERIDAL and SARD search-and-rescue datasets. Three detectors, Faster R-CNN, YOLOv11, and RT-DETR, were evaluated across 168 conditions. Under low light, all three detectors achieved zero recall on both datasets, and this failure produced no warning signal. The authors release the corruption engine, evaluation pipeline, and per-condition results as an audit tool. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit drone person detection across 168 disaster-like conditions with three detectors, reporting zero recall in low light and confirmation on real night images.

entry.title: Testing floor plan generators against real architectural acceptance rules
entry.summary: Where Generated Floor Plans Stop: Encoding Practice Acceptance Rules to Evaluate Machine Learning Floor Plan Generators arXiv · Oct 14, 2026Machine learning floor plan generators are usually judged by how well room adjacencies match a request, which ignores architectural knowledge. The authors encode an architecture practice's acceptance rules as six checks applied in a fixed order, calibrating two room-shape limits so each rejects 5 per cent of built apartments. Applied to four published generators and the RPLAN and MSD datasets, the checks stop the generators at different points. The checker is released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors encode an architecture practice's floor plan acceptance rules as six ordered checks to evaluate generators beyond adjacency metrics, reporting results on four generators and two built corp

entry.title: RoboArchitect: Automatically Designing Robot Agents with Persistent Memory
entry.summary: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents RoboArchitect, a system in which a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the control harness around a frozen robot policy. Without updating any model weights, average success rises from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks across multiple benchmarks and policies. The evolved harness also develops persistent memory that carries learned experience into later decisions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors automate harness design around a frozen robot policy, reporting large success gains on unseen scenes and tasks across benchmarks.

entry.title: Subquadratic attention using a hierarchical tree indexer for long contexts
entry.summary: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), a sparse attention method that replaces the quadratic cost of standard attention with a tree-structured indexer. The method builds a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which queries traverse top-down to retrieve a sparse set of keys. The authors report that ZHA can be applied to existing pretrained models with a short KL distillation stage and maintains performance on long-context and reasoning tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hierarchical tree indexer for sub-quadratic sparse attention, distilled into pretrained models and evaluated on retrieval, reasoning, and coding tasks.

entry.title: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression: examines how robust regression methods perform in excess risk (regret) under distribution shift, comparing several approaches.
entry.summary: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for multivariate least-squares regression when the source and target distributions differ by an adversarial 2-Wasserstein perturbation of size ε. It characterizes the small-ε complexity with a problem-specific condition number κ, showing that simple methods including DRO attain the instance-optimal rate O(κε²). The authors identify settings where DRO is provably suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors, and propose minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR), which attain the minimax rate. Exact convex reformulation, an accelerated algorithm, high-probability guarantees, and numerical experiments are provided. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show DRO can be suboptimal in regret and that MRO and SNR attain the minimax rate, with a convex reformulation and an accelerated proximal algorithm.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving synthetic data via noisy sliced Chebyshev moments
entry.summary: Differentially Private Synthetic Data from Sliced Chebyshev Moments arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces SPLICE, a differentially private synthetic data algorithm that measures noisy sliced Chebyshev polynomial moments of a target distribution and fits a distribution to match them. For a dataset of n examples and constant privacy parameters, the authors prove the output's Sliced Wasserstein-1 distance to the target is Õ(1/√n), a bound independent of data dimension. The method reportedly achieves state-of-the-art performance against prior differentially private synthetic data methods on an extensive benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present SPLICE, a dimension-independent Sliced Wasserstein bound for DP synthetic data from noisy Chebyshev moments, compared against prior methods on a benchmark.

entry.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
entry.summary: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to choose stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient descent on smooth convex problems, assuming zero-mean gradient noise with bounded variance. It gives an exact worst-case analysis of the expected suboptimality of the final iterate for any N stepsizes in [0,1.5]. When the variance bound is at least order 1/√N, it identifies the minimax optimal schedule, proves its uniqueness, and shows the optimal stepsizes decrease monotonically. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact worst-case analysis of SGD's final-iterate suboptimality, prove uniqueness of the minimax optimal stepsize schedule, and rule out fractal accelerations.

entry.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing How Six LLMs' Smoking-Cessation Advice Varies by User Persona
entry.summary: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The authors asked six widely used large language models from four providers the same four smoking-cessation questions, posed by twelve user personas differing in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, yielding 2,880 responses. Models mentioned FDA-approved prescription cessation drugs 32 to 67 percentage points less often for teen personas than adult personas, and five of six models gave fewer facts to personas claiming healthcare expertise. The study also tested a system prompt specifying a factual floor, which narrowed persona differences but produced effects that varied across models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit six LLMs with persona variation on smoking-cessation advice, test a factual-floor system prompt across 2,880 responses, and release all responses and analysis code.

entry.title: Learning clean image generation from only noisy measurements
entry.summary: Learning Clean Generative Processes from Noisy Measurements arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to train a generative model of clean images using only noisy observations. The authors show that Noise2Noise regression can learn posterior predictions from independent noisy views, but only at or above the training noise level. To cover lower noise levels, they impose a consistency condition and derive when it uniquely determines the path to the clean distribution. Experiments on CIFAR-10, photon-counting microscopy, and synthetic aperture radar show that the consistency relation repairs the sampling process beyond the data's noise level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a consistency constraint to learn posterior predictions below the training noise level and derive conditions for uniquely recovering clean image distributions, reporting tests on CIFAR

entry.title: GhostPrefix: Universal Audio Prefix Attacks That Manipulate Speech Recognition Without Syncing
entry.summary: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces GhostPrefix, a universal adversarial attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. It learns a short, reusable audio segment that is prepended to live speech, so it can influence ASR outputs without knowing the upcoming utterance or aligning with it in time. The authors test three attack modes across 13 open-source ASR models and report high success rates in both digital and over-the-air settings. They also show that the resulting errors affect downstream tools such as voice assistants and AI note-taking applications. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first synchronization-free universal audio prefix attack, evaluated on 13 ASR models in digital and over-the-air settings across three attack modes.

entry.title: New lower bounds on sample needs for private PAC learning
entry.summary: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy and presents a framework for proving lower bounds on sample complexity. It constructs classes with identical VC and Littlestone dimensions but different private sample complexities, showing these dimensions alone do not determine the sample complexity. The authors introduce the Independent Class Packing parameter and prove that any private PAC learner, even an improper one, needs Ω(ICP/(αε)) examples. Using this framework, they obtain tight bounds for axis-aligned rectangles, unions of intervals and linear subspaces, and improved bounds for halfspaces and convex polygons. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Independent Class Packing and prove lower bounds for private PAC learning, reporting tight bounds for rectangles, unions of intervals, and subspaces.

entry.title: Robust learning of multi-index models under logconcave distributions using weak partial learners
entry.summary: Robust Learning of Multi-Index Models under Logconcave Distributions via Weak Partial Learners arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents a new algorithmic framework for learning Boolean concept classes under logconcave distributions, applicable to broad families of multi-index models and extendable to partial classification and testable learning. Its core is a boosting approach built on weak partial learners, which uses a recursive moment-based partitioning procedure and a method for detecting moment discrepancies to construct the required weak learner. The authors obtain faster robust learners for concept classes such as functions of halfspaces and multiclass linear classifiers under logconcave marginals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a boosting framework using weak partial learners plus a moment-based partitioning and discrepancy-finding method, reporting faster robust learners for multi-index models under logc

entry.title: Mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces
entry.summary: On k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression when features take values in a metric space. It analyzes how neighbor selection redistributes probability and gives separate conditions for the approximation error and the conditional response variance. Under a finite fourth response moment with k_n tending to infinity and k_n/n tending to zero, a uniform L2 bound on the selection densities suffices. The authors also construct a space satisfying sigma-finite Nagata dimensionality on which the mean squared error of a fixed noiseless response with all finite moments diverges, showing that this dimensional condition does not guarantee mean squared consistency for unbounded responses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize k-NN regression mean squared consistency to metric spaces, give selection-density bounds, and construct a counterexample with divergent error.

entry.title: "A Patch is More Than a Token": A Multi-State View of Vision Transformer Patch Representations
entry.summary: A Patch is More Than a Token arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that Vision Transformers represent each image patch with a single canonical token, which captures only one state of that patch. The authors propose PMTT, a framework that builds a family of representation states and an analytic Manifold on frozen DINOv3 backbones. Across six visual capabilities and four model scales, the results show that pretrained backbones hold richer patch information than the standard single-token interface exposes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend a single canonical patch token to a state family and manifold, reporting gains over observed states on frozen DINOv3 with 4,096 anchors.

entry.title: ∇Mimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control via Differentiable Simulation
entry.summary: nablaMimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control with Differentiable Simulation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents ∇Mimic, a method that trains humanoid robot control policies using exact gradients from a simulator instead of relying on sample-hungry reinforcement learning. It uses per-sample gradient clipping and multistep regression to control exploding gradients and reuse costly simulation windows. The authors also release NablaEngine, a differentiable GPU simulator for the Unitree G1 that they report is 11.5 times faster than the MuJoCo Warp adjoint. On whole-body tracking of 40 LAFAN1 clips, the method reaches a score of 0.82 in 20 minutes and 0.874 in 1.8 hours. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose gradient clipping and multistep regression to tame exploding exact gradients, evaluated on G1 humanoid whole-body tracking with open-source release.

entry.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging: A Gaussian-process method that builds whole-domain PDE residuals into its covariance for solving PDEs
entry.summary: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK), a Gaussian process method for solving partial differential equations. It is built on a PDE-residual kernel whose inner product is the L² inner product of PDE residuals, so the posterior mean has minimum integrated squared PDE residual without a separate residual-weight parameter. Under stated regularity and stability conditions, the authors establish H²-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, and numerical studies support the theory and PDE-solving capability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a PDE-residual kernel using the L2 inner product of residuals, deriving convergence rates and a nonasymptotic bound verified numerically.

entry.title: Infinite ResNets as Gaussian Mean ODEs: a simple continuous model of how very large residual networks train
entry.summary: Infinite ResNets are Gaussian Mean ODEs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how deep residual networks (ResNets) train when width, depth, and embedding, input, and output dimensions all grow large. Earlier work used dynamical mean field theory, which yields hard-to-analyze non-Markovian dynamics. The authors instead show that, under standard shape scalings and a 1/depth branch scaling, gradient descent in the limit is gradient descent on a Neural Mean ODE with Gaussian initial weights. They derive approximation scaling laws that depend on the network shape and the data covariance spectrum, and also cover Mixture of Experts models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors replace non-Markovian DMFT dynamics with GD on a Gaussian-initialized Neural Mean ODE, reporting approximation scaling laws in the joint large-limit.

entry.title: A randomized study testing an AI tool that helps patients prepare for doctor visits
entry.summary: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study designed a large language model-based agent to help patients get ready for clinical appointments by gathering health context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant information, and building prioritized question lists. In a randomized study in the Google Health app, 802 U.S. adults had 866 health conversations with the agent (standard or concise variant) or a minimally prompted control chatbot. The agent significantly outperformed the control in blinded clinician reviews and patient self-reports while maintaining high medical safety and appropriateness. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a randomized study of 802 adults comparing a structured LLM visit-preparation agent with a control chatbot, showing higher readiness and satisfaction.

entry.title: Anomalies as Residuals: Cauchy Displacement Networks (a compact network for tabular anomaly detection)
entry.summary: Anomalies as Residuals: Cauchy Displacement Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes the Cauchy Displacement Network (CDN), a single-hidden-layer network with Cauchy activations that learns to predict each normal point's displacement toward the mean of its k nearest training neighbours, scoring queries by the length of that predicted displacement. It needs only one forward pass per query and its size does not depend on the training set. On 46 benchmark datasets against 28 baselines, CDN achieves the best mean rank under both AUC-ROC and AUC-PR while running much faster on a single CPU thread. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compile neighbourhood geometry into a single-pass Cauchy network, prove exact Student-t score representation and an approximation bound, and report best mean rank across 46 datasets versus

entry.title: Predicting whether text spans contain evidence online, without repeat queries
entry.summary: Online Evidence-Containment Prediction over Text Spans under Distinct Queries arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies sequential verification of nested text regions in evidence-grounded NLP systems, where each candidate is predicted before exact verification and queried at most once. The authors formalize this as Online Evidence-Containment Prediction (OECP), framing span containment as distinct-query online isotonic regression with regret bounds. On Natural Questions, containment gives a large deductive gain and a smaller learned gain on unresolved candidates. The Expected Search-space Reduction (ESR) method uses these predictions to localize evidence with fewer verifier calls. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize span containment as online isotonic regression over a 2D product order, giving regret bounds and evaluating on NQ, SciFact, ERASER, and DPR hierarchies.

entry.title: Subliminal reinforcement learning: a trait passes through a judge's scores
entry.summary: Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies whether a student model trained only on its own outputs and a language-model judge's scores picks up a trait. The judge is made to prefer one animal, and the student, writing invented syllables or numbers, shifts its preference toward that animal. The authors describe the transfer as a four-stage chain and report that the same chain holds for AI-safety dispositions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show trait transfer via language-model judge scores in RL post-training, proposing a four-stage chain, tested across 48 design cells with false-discovery control.

entry.title: A general method for estimating the probability of events defined by data
entry.summary: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how to estimate the probability an unknown distribution assigns to an event determined by a sample through a known mapping, using only that sample. This framework covers missing mass, targets in adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, and the test error of a predictor trained on the data. The authors analyze the empirical plug-in estimator and the leave-one-out estimator, which recovers the Good–Turing estimator. They also propose a hybrid estimator for a predictor combining a base classifier with memorized exceptions, and give two error bounds for it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a unified framework for estimating data-dependent event probabilities, with an adaptive missing mass estimator and two error bounds.

entry.title: Corroborative Learning: Models Strengthen Each Other by Reconstructing Task Responses
entry.summary: Corroborative Learning: Mutual Enhancement through Task-Response Reconstruction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes Corroborative Learning (CL), a method in which independently trained models on the same task improve one another while keeping their differences. Each model reconstructs response increments from its collaborator's representations across disjoint groups, selectively constraining directions by how well they can be reconstructed, without direct output or feature matching. Across six language tasks, 24 models, and 36 pairs, CL outperforms capacity-matched independent adaptation on every task. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a cross-group reconstruction paradigm for complementary collaboration, report a PSD regularizer interpretation, and compare across 24 models and 36 pairs.

entry.title: TinyAstral: Moving Self-Improving Agent Harnesses into Small Robot Manipulation Models
entry.summary: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how improvements to the harness (tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic) of a large vision-language robot teacher can be transferred to a compact agent. The method first refines the teacher's harness through recursive self-improvement, accepting edits only when they pass a paired statistical test, then distills a 4B student model that runs in the same harness. On the RoboTwin benchmark, the teacher's success rate rises from 33.4% to 63.6%, and the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report distilling a self-evolved harness into a 4B student, reaching 62.8% on RoboTwin versus the teacher's 63.6%, with about one fifth of its accelerator time.

entry.title: Researcher-guided evolutionary discovery of entanglement-assisted quantum code families
entry.summary: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a pipeline that combines LLM-guided program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, certified nonexistence checks, and formal proof checking, with researchers in the loop. It is applied to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs), where evolved programs gave finite qubit constructions that were generalized into the code family [[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q, with the underlying algebraic certificate checked in Lean. The authors report that this family, together with entanglement lifting, closes 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables. The released evidence includes 115 verified code records and ten nonexistence results with checked DRAT proofs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize evolved finite constructions into an infinite code family, proved with Lean, closing 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables.

entry.title: When AI Agents Should Ask: Clarification Requests When Human Attention Is Limited
entry.summary: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies when AI agents working in parallel should ask a shared human for missing information rather than searching for it themselves. The authors build a simplified model, formulate it as a dynamic program, and propose the Pairwise Coordination Policy (PCP). On 864 synthetic cases, PCP's mean gap to optimal cost is 0.07%, and it cuts cost by 18-31% versus three standard asking rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model multi-agent clarification under shared human attention as a dynamic program and propose PCP, reporting near-optimal results on 864 synthetic cases and an LLM case study.

entry.title: MotorSense: a paired video and muscle-signal dataset for understanding hand actions
entry.summary: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces MotorSense, a large-scale dataset pairing egocentric video with surface electromyography (EMG) signals, covering 100 hours of unscripted bimanual manipulation. The authors use cross-modal pre-training between video and EMG to learn sensorimotor-aligned visual representations. These representations are transferred to action recognition, 3D hand reconstruction, and 3D contact reconstruction. The paper also shows EMG signals conditioning a video diffusion model to generate fine-grained hand manipulation videos. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a large paired egocentric video and EMG dataset and report cross-modal pre-training outperforms baselines on four action tasks.

entry.title: PRISM-Net: A Routing Network That Separates Line and Color Features for Explainable Product Image Search
entry.summary: PRISM-Net: Dynamic Routing Network with VLM-Guided Disentangled Attribute Distillation for Explainable Fine-Grained Product Retrieval arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper presents PRISM-Net, a multi-expert network for fine-grained e-commerce product retrieval that splits visual features into line (structure) and color expert pathways. A meta-router adaptively fuses these with base features, and the experts are supervised by zero-shot text prompts from SigLIP, avoiding manual attribute labels. Across 5-fold cross-validation on 275,454 images, product mAP@10 on SwinV2 rises from 80.98% to 83.90%.

entry.title: Compositional Self-Improvement: Promises and Pitfalls
entry.summary: Compositional Self-Improvement: Promises and Pitfalls arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether models can use compositional structure to create training labels for harder problems by combining their predictions on simpler subproblems. Controlled experiments identify three failure modes: unreliable subproblem predictions, errors introduced by composition, and limited supervision coverage. In more realistic coding and reasoning tasks, composed labels are more accurate than direct self-generated labels and improve performance even on longer compositions than seen in training, though the same failure modes remain visible.

entry.title: From Lookups to Lessons: Turning Retrieved Knowledge into Parametric Memory
entry.summary: From Lookups to Lessons: Turning Retrieved Knowledge into Parametric Memory arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces ResMem, which has a language model read retrieved text offline to produce teacher targets, then trains a parametric memory to learn an additive logit residual that aligns a same-backbone student with the teacher. The method avoids storing large token representations, unlike kNN-datastore memory approaches. On a Wikipedia subset it cuts the storage retained for teacher construction by 94.7% compared with the evaluated kNN pipeline. Across five question answering datasets, mean token F1 rises from 32.83% for the frozen LLM to 34.48%, and it breaks 21% fewer correct answers than a kNN-trained memory.

entry.title: SpBench: An Agent-Native Framework for Benchmarking Lakehouse Engines Across Platforms
entry.summary: SpBench: An Agent-Native Framework for Cross-Engine Lakehouse Benchmarking arXiv · Oct 31, 2026SpBench is a framework for benchmarking lakehouse data engines across platforms, and it is already in production use for Snowpark and Snowpark Connect for Apache Spark. It runs standardized suites such as TPCx-BB and TPC-DI alongside custom benchmarks drawn from production workloads, detecting performance regressions on a continuous basis. The paper introduces a typed, code-generated benchmark substrate, a structured telemetry contract that lets LLM agents query results, and an agent-native harness of three composable skills. The authors report that this architecture enabled over 400 benchmark queries and that regressions it caught led to production improvements.

entry.title: Quantile-based calibration of LLM judge scores against human ratings
entry.summary: Quantiles, Not Points: Streaming Quantile Matching for Ordinal-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper addresses the distributional shift between LLM-as-a-judge scores and human ratings, which post-hoc calibration on a small labeled anchor set aims to correct. The authors treat LLM scores as ordinal ratings drawn from a distribution and propose streaming quantile matching (SQM), which computes the optimal-transport map between LLM and human score distributions. Their evaluation reports that SQM respects the ordinality of the human anchor set and achieves the best distributional fidelity and top overall rank across models and data. The paper also notes that post-hoc calibration narrows the raw error gap between smaller and larger judge models.

entry.title: Analog and hybrid computing in the 21st century: a look at computing that uses physical circuit signals, not just digital logic, for simulation, optimization and energy-efficient AI
entry.summary: Analog and hybrid computing in the 21st century arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This interdisciplinary paper reviews modern analog and hybrid (analog-digital) computing. Analog computers represent mathematical variables and relations with physical quantities, such as electronic circuit signals, and can directly represent nonlinear dynamical systems. The authors note that the design constraints of digital architectures increasingly limit performance and energy efficiency, while analog systems can map specific computations onto physical processes using smaller, simpler elements. The article discusses applications in simulating dynamical systems, performing optimization, and enabling more energy-efficient artificial intelligence.

entry.title: CLiS: Training-free TPU attention speedup for video diffusion via certified stabilization
entry.summary: CLiS: Plug-and-Play Attention Acceleration for Video Diffusion on TPUs via Certified Stabilization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the slow attention computation in high-resolution video diffusion models, which operate over long token sequences. It proposes CLiS, a training-free, plug-and-play method that fixes per-row stabilizers before the key-value loop and certifies numerical safety per attention head, reverting to online softmax when certification fails. On Wan 2.2 and LTX-2 running on TPUs, CLiS reduces diffusion transformer step latency by up to 19.6% compared with tuned online softmax, without measurable quality loss.

entry.title: Accuracy Drops With Table Size, Not Dialogue Turns: Data Delivery in an Agent
entry.summary: Fidelity Collapses with Table Size, Not Turn Count: Delivery Architecture in a Deployed Tool-Using Agent arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper compares two ways of passing a tool's structured records to a multi-turn agent: putting full record sets into the model's context, or keeping them in session state and delivering rows through a typed side channel. Across 24 dialogues, the side-channel design answered 92.3% of turns fully correctly, versus 45.7% for the context design. The context design's accuracy collapses as the delivered table grows beyond about 74 rows.

entry.title: Designing human-AI teamwork rules that account for how people are swayed by AI outputs
entry.summary: OmniMechanism Design for Human-AI Collaboration with Impressionable Minds arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces a framework called collaborative omnimechanism design for human-AI collaboration, recognizing that human judgments can be influenced by how AI outputs are presented. It is built on a computationally efficient contextual bandit variant of boosting for outcome indistinguishability, reducing a calibration-type condition to weighted calibration. The authors evaluate the approach in three collaboration settings and report that it adapts to different query costs and prediction objectives without retraining, performing comparably to or better than the baselines.

entry.title: Local Spatial TreeSHAP: A Geographically Explainable AI Study of Urbanization-Dependent Flood Resilience Heterogeneity
entry.summary: Local Spatial TreeSHAP: Geographically Explainable AI Revealing Urbanization-Dependent Spatial Heterogeneity in Flood Resilience arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a spatially explainable machine learning framework combining geographically weighted random forests with a new Local Spatial TreeSHAP algorithm to interpret flood resilience mechanisms at the community level. It is applied to 779 communities affected by the July 2023 extreme rainstorm in Beijing. The results show resilience mechanisms vary spatially more strongly than the underlying physical and socio-economic conditions, and identify three distinct resilience regimes across an urbanization gradient.

entry.title: Real-VAS: A Real-World Video Amodal Segmentation Dataset
entry.summary: Real-VAS: a Real-World Video Amodal Segmentation Dataset arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents Real-VAS, a large-scale zero-shot evaluation dataset for amodal segmentation of occluded objects in video, built by compositing real-image video clips. Its generation pipeline derives the object mask, occlusion boundary, and composited image from a single unoccluded source, producing consistent ground truth without human estimation or costly 3D reconstruction. The dataset covers dynamic occlusion and container scenarios, including on-surface, articulated, and mobile containment, where object motion is simulated from the container's tracked transformation. The authors state that the dataset and generation code will be made publicly available.

entry.title: Do multimodal AI models give consistent answers about the same optical spectrum in different formats?
entry.summary: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The study tests whether multimodal models reach the same decision when one optical spectrum is shown as a table or plot in nanometers or photon energy. It also checks whether models answer "undetermined" when needed data are missing, using measured spectra of silicon metasurfaces and gold nanoparticles. Changing only the representation shifted accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model.

entry.title: PAM-Mamba: An Efficient Mamba-Based Method for Dense Action Detection
entry.summary: PAM-Mamba - Efficient Dense Action Detection using Mamba arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents PAM-Mamba, a method for precisely locating multiple overlapping actions in long untrimmed videos. It builds a linear-time O(T) multi-branch temporal encoder on Mamba, with components such as gated learnable positional encoding and bidirectional temporal Mamba. On Charades and MultiTHUMOS it reports 26.82 to 46.92 mAP with 26.1 to 27.9M parameters, 61% to 63% fewer than PAT.

entry.title: A paper viewing neural network layer convergence through a spectral renormalization-group lens
entry.summary: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper uses Wilsonian renormalization-group ideas to explain the heavy-tailed power-law spectra that deep neural network layers develop during training, focusing on exponents near 2. It offers statistical and physical interpretations of this value. The authors introduce the SETOL theory, a spectral RG flow connecting HTSR and SETOL to optimizers such as Muon, and a new optimizer extension, WW-PGD.

entry.title: RankLane: Faster Mixture-of-Experts Prefill on Accelerators via Load-Ranked Expert Lanes
entry.summary: RankLane: Efficient MoE Prefill on Accelerators with Ranked Expert Capacities arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents RankLane, a method for running mixture-of-experts (MoE) model prefill on accelerators with static execution plans. It ranks each device's experts by current load and assigns them to fixed-capacity lanes, using runtime indices to select experts and token rows. Evaluated on four Cloud AI 100 Ultra SoCs with Qwen3-30B-A3B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B, it reports end-to-end prefill speedups of 1.27-4.18x and 1.93-3.46x over a dense baseline, respectively.

entry.title: Circuit Oracle: answering questions about model internals by automated attribution graph analysis
entry.summary: Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Circuit Oracle, a large language model with a multi-agent harness and task-specific skills that answers natural-language questions by reading attribution graphs through tool calls. It is tested on three safety-relevant tasks: detecting spurious features, eliciting hidden knowledge from taboo-finetuned models, and suppressing refusals through feature-level interventions. On spurious-feature detection it reaches 78.2 ± 2.4% accuracy, beating single-layer ranking baselines, while trained self-explainers remain stronger for secret elicitation. Results are mixed; on refusal suppression it roughly matches a diff-in-means baseline only with best-of-five attempts.

entry.title: Non-conformal distortion and local orientation reversal in a Transformer's Fourier modular-addition circuit
entry.summary: Nonconformal Distortion and Local Orientation Reversal in the Fourier Circuit of a Modular-Addition Transformer arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper examines the local geometry of a Fourier-based modular-addition circuit in a one-layer Transformer. For each of five key frequencies, the MLP contribution is restricted to the corresponding Fourier input plane and its directional Beltrami coefficient is measured under continuous input perturbations. Trained maps show nonconformal distortion and regions of local orientation reversal, with the median Beltrami coefficient falling from 0.939 at initialization to 0.390 after training.

entry.title: How Wording of AI Red-Teaming Instructions Shapes Test Results
entry.summary: On the Framing Effect of AI Red-Teaming Instructions: Evidence from Prior Exercises and Controlled Simulations arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether the wording of instructions used in AI red-teaming, which probes generative AI systems for harms, affects the results. The authors reviewed 228 prior works and then ran controlled simulations that varied only the instructions while holding risk domain, attacker, and target model fixed, totaling 22,500 attacks. They find that risk granularity, instruction length, the presence of examples, and explicit harm definitions significantly predict attack success rates.

entry.title: TileWeave: Heterogeneous Tiling for Fast Sparse Prefill on Phones
entry.summary: TileWeave: Heterogeneous Tiling for Sparse Prefill on Mobile SoCs arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents TileWeave, a method for speeding up the prefill stage of large language models on smartphones, where long inputs cause high latency and memory use. It splits sparse attention by how much key blocks are reused across queries: heavily shared blocks run on the NPU in coarse tiles, while low-reuse blocks run on the GPU only for the queries that selected them. On RULER and LongBench, its accuracy matches or exceeds XAttention, and on two Snapdragon phones it achieves 1.35 to 3.23 times faster full-model prefill than XAttention.

entry.title: Is It Cheating or Just Failing? A Stronger LLM Monitor Separates Reward Hacking From Honest Mistakes
entry.summary: Hacking or Just Failing? A More Capable LLM Monitor Better Separates Reward Hacking from Honest Failure arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies whether an AI agent's inflated score comes from gaming the scoring system or from ordinary mistakes, using a sandboxed task with labelled episodes. Small local monitors failed to separate exploits from honest failures, while Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite met the pre-registered criterion (AUC 0.80) on the same inputs, though with only 14 exploit episodes the estimate is uncertain. The authors also report that a two-rule deterministic check caught every known exploit and release their environment, labels and logs.

entry.title: TAP-Out: Tracking Points Anywhere in 360° Using Video Outpainting
entry.summary: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360deg via Outpainting arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents TAP-Out, an offline method for tracking points that leave the camera's field of view. It uses generative video outpainting to extend a narrow-view video into a full 360° panoramic video, locates target objects with video object segmentation, and produces object-centred perspective crops for standard in-frame trackers. On the TAPVid360 benchmark, TAP-Out achieves state-of-the-art results, improving out-of-view tracking accuracy by about 3x over the best prior method.

entry.title: MXCode: Vector Quantization for Efficient MX-Native LLM Inference
entry.summary: MXCode: Vector Quantization for MX-Native Inference at Scale arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces MXCode, a framework that combines roughly 2-bit-per-weight vector quantization with MX-native FP4 computation to reduce memory and bandwidth demands in large language model inference. It proposes three strategies, PostScale, PreScale, and PreScale+, which trade off quantization quality, scale overhead, and codebook granularity. The authors evaluate MXCode on Qwen3 (235B), DeepSeek-R1 (671B), and GLM-5.2 (753B), and report memory and time-to-first-token results on GB300 hardware.

entry.title: Comparing SAM-based Transformers and CNNs for Segmenting Thin Retinal Blood Vessels
entry.summary: Evaluating SAM-based and Convolutional Architectures in Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation: Model Capacity, Computational Cost and Foundation Pre-training arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper compares a plain Vision Transformer encoder (MedSAM), a hybrid Transformer (LiteMedSAM), and three CNNs of different sizes on retinal vessel segmentation across DRIVE, HRF, and FIVES, with a microscopy dataset (VessMap) as a second-domain check. The authors measured centerline recall and precision for thin vessels, along with computational cost and training epochs. They found the pre-trained MedSAM's thin-vessel centerline recall was not significantly different from the best CNN on all four datasets. A compact plain ViT found by architecture search but trained from scratch did not match this performance.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning for Phase I Dose Allocation
entry.summary: Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning for Phase I Dose Allocation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a single reinforcement-learning policy for Phase I dose-finding trials with varying numbers of ordered dose levels, representing each dose as a token processed by a Transformer encoder. The policy chooses among de-escalation, staying, or escalation, while the final maximum tolerated dose is selected outside the policy using weighted isotonic regression and a safety cap. Simulations show that toxicity-penalized policies reduce dose-limiting toxicity burden, whereas unpenalized policies improve selection accuracy at greater toxicity cost. The authors state that superiority over conventional dose-finding designs is not established.

entry.title: CalVLA: Training Robot Policies to Signal Their Own Likely Failures
entry.summary: CalVLA: Shaping Native Confidence in Vision-Language-Action Policies with Outcome Supervision arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper presents CalVLA, a method that adjusts the native action-token confidence of the OpenVLA-7B vision-language-action policy using successful and failed rollouts and an Action-Confidence Alignment loss, without an auxiliary failure detector. On a held-out test split from 500 LIBERO-10 configurations, the adapted confidence reaches a failure-discrimination AUROC of 0.7392 ± 0.0480 over three seeds, up from 0.4485 before adaptation. Mean task success falls from 58% to 55%, and the authors state that the results show improved failure discrimination only, not improved control or established safety benefits.

entry.title: Risk assessment and optimal design for AI-agent safeguard systems that account for dependence between safeguards
entry.summary: Dependence-Aware Risk Assessment and Optimal Design of AI-Agent Safeguard Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a framework for assessing risk in multi-component AI safeguard systems by accounting for dependence among safeguard decisions. It jointly selects configurations and operating policies for sequential layered screening and selective verification, and provides stochastic comparisons of error probabilities and costs. The authors release DAPOA, an open-source package implementing the framework. Numerical experiments show that independence-based selections violate security requirements in six of eight scenarios, and an empirical study with four LLM safeguards finds dependence-aware selection lowers held-out total cost by 39.6%.

entry.title: An agent system for the ML training lifecycle covering model generation, validation, and optimization
entry.summary: Agent Stack for ML Training Lifecycle: Generation, Validation, and Optimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents an agent stack deployed at LinkedIn with two independently usable loops: AutoTorch, which generates and migrates PyTorch models and training pipelines, and AutoResearch, which optimizes models through expert-steered or autonomous experiments. AutoTorch uses executable validation hooks to iteratively repair its outputs before engineer review and full-scale training. Across 115 workflow runs, AutoTorch completed generation and full-scale training in 92, and 77 of those met post-training quality requirements. In a separate cohort of 100 production pipelines, AutoResearch improved the primary task metric on held-out data for 28. The authors estimate that elapsed end-to-end migration time fell from about eight weeks to two weeks.

entry.title: LF-VideoQA: A benchmark testing long-video understanding with long-form theory-of-mind questions
entry.summary: LF-VideoQA: Evaluating Long-Video Understanding with Long-Form Theory-of-Mind Questions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces LF-VideoQA, a dataset for open-ended, long-form question answering about long narrative videos. Its questions test theory of mind, requiring models to combine evidence spread across the video. The dataset includes over 6,300 questions on 94 recent films, each with a rubric for scoring recall and precision. Experiments show the task is very difficult, even for a model with access to the screenplay, with recall being the main bottleneck.

entry.title: MoRE-GS: Routing Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: MoRE-GS: Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents MoRE-GS, a framework for forecasting future views of dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. It reconstructs a Gaussian representation from only the observed temporal prefix and predicts control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid constraints. A routing table and persistence gate combine the experts' outputs, and the authors report improved performance over other methods on D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes.

entry.title: Unlearning via extrapolated shrink-and-heal lookahead
entry.summary: Unlearning by Extrapolating a Shrink-and-Heal Lookahead arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies unlearning in large language models, aiming to make a model behave like one retrained without its forget set. The proposed method, SHIFT, shrinks the fine-tuned model toward its pre-fine-tuning weights and briefly relearns the retain set to remove forget-specific effects. It extrapolates the lookahead's per-token changes into distillation targets and refines them iteratively. Under a unified OpenUnlearning protocol against eleven baselines, SHIFT achieves the highest aggregate score on all TOFU settings and the closest alignment with the oracle, and it preserves the most retain knowledge on MUSE.

entry.title: Reusing Entity-Replacement Responses Across Prompts: Tests whether internal changes from entity replacement in one English factual question transfer to another question about the same entity, with model weights fixed.
entry.summary: Cross-Prompt Reuse of Entity-Replacement Responses arXiv · Oct 31, 2026With weights fixed, the paper adds hidden-state changes from two source questions to a target question about the same entity and compares this with direct reuse of output-score changes. Using other-relation sources, hidden reuse removes part of the no-change error on small models, but on small plain-format checkpoints it mainly reproduces the shift both relations share rather than reliably lowering relation-selective error. Applying the same relation-neutral change at both questions' entity tokens lowers relation-selective error more than random or other-replacement changes, suggesting dependence on the receiving question.

entry.title: SIEVE: Compressing Visual Tokens Across Multiple Images While Keeping Each Image's Evidence
entry.summary: SIEVE: Preserving Cross-Image Evidence via Depth-Aware Token Compression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents SIEVE, a training-free, single-pass method for compressing visual tokens in vision-language models that process multiple images. It pools each image into a compact grid, selects representative tokens using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas, and merges unselected tokens into similar representatives within the same image. The authors report that SIEVE achieves the highest average scores at a 6.25% token budget across several multi-image and single-image benchmarks, and on LLaVA-OneVision-7B it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points at a 12.5% budget with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.

entry.title: Limits of Test-Time Compute for Model Self-Evaluation
entry.summary: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper finds that adding more candidate answers does not consistently close the gap between final-answer accuracy and pass@N. It measures how well models separate their correct and incorrect generations using ranking error, which it decomposes into bias and variance components. Based on this analysis, the authors propose Scorpio, a method that jointly scores randomly grouped candidates, and report gains in verification, tree search, and aggregation on math, code, and puzzle benchmarks.

entry.title: Queering the Audits: Community-Based Auditing of AI Harms to Queer Communities
entry.summary: Queering the Audits: Community-Based Auditing of AI Harms to Queer Communities arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a participatory auditing approach for finding harms that AI systems cause to queer communities, such as erasure, misclassification, and discrimination. The authors ran a workshop at EurIPS 2025 where 16 queer community members audited four case studies using the 4Cs harm taxonomy (Content, Conduct, Contact, Contract). Participants traced most harms to problem definition and data collection, and found contracts that extract value from vulnerable groups while offering little recourse.

entry.title: SPARK: Self-Correcting Embodied Memory via Physical Re-Observation
entry.summary: SPARK: Self-Correcting Embodied Memory via Physical Re-Observation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026SPARK is a multi-episode framework that corrects errors in retrieval-augmented memory used by embodied agents. After an initial episode, a semantic critic flags problematic regions of the knowledge base, a planner generates targeted revisits, and selective merging adds, removes, or replaces information. Tested on four outdoor AirSim maps under two degraded viewpoint conditions, one corrective episode improved embodied question answering on every map while storing 13-41% fewer objects than append-only updating. Extending correction through Episode 4 brought every map above its undegraded reference performance.

entry.title: DEPLOY-RL: Certifying Reinforcement Learning Controllers for Safety-Critical Industrial Processes
entry.summary: DEPLOY-RL: Active Boundary Discovery and Conservative Certification for Deployable Reinforcement Learning in Safety-Critical Continuous Processes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents DEPLOY-RL, a post-training framework for deciding whether a reinforcement learning policy is safe to deploy in safety-critical continuous processes. It focuses on finding where failures occur rather than measuring performance everywhere, using a sampling method that concentrates on certification-critical boundaries. The framework uses conformal risk control for finite-sample false-go guarantees and a Deploy/No-Deploy/Abstain decision with a PID/MPC fallback. In simulations on a papermaking digital twin and the Tennessee Eastman benchmark, it reports a 4.4% false-go rate while retaining 88.6% policy coverage.

entry.title: Using graph neural networks to classify large Boolean functions under NPN equivalence
entry.summary: Efficient NPN Classification for Large Functions using Graph Neural Network arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies NPN classification, which determines whether Boolean functions can be transformed into one another by negating or permuting inputs and negating the output. Exact methods require exhaustive enumeration whose cost grows exponentially with the number of inputs. The authors recast the task as NPN action prediction and use a bidirectional heterogeneous graph neural network on AND-Inverter Graphs to predict negations and permutations, supported by graph rewriting. Experiments show the prediction is learnable, improves over heuristic baselines, and scales to functions with up to 16 inputs.

entry.title: Breaking irregular time series into interpretable temporal patterns using mixture-of-experts
entry.summary: Decomposing Irregular Time Series into Interpretable Temporal Patterns with Mixture-of-Experts arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces MoTIF, a framework that uses mixture-of-experts attention to split irregularly spaced sequential data into cyclical and range-based temporal patterns spanning minutes to years. On synthetic data and a public credit card transaction dataset, MoTIF outperforms baselines on next-value and next-amount prediction. Its learned routing also shows that fraudulent transactions have bursty, calendar-agnostic timing compared with the steadier periodicity of legitimate ones. The authors argue this approach keeps predictive accuracy while making sequence models more auditable.

entry.title: C3: Speech-guided cache retrieval for faster long-audio processing in speech models
entry.summary: C3: Speech-Guided KV Retrieval for Long-Context SpeechLLM Inference arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Speech language models store audio far more densely than text, so their attention cache dominates memory and compute during long generations. The paper proposes C3 (Cluster-Compete-Compete), which indexes audio cache entries hierarchically, has query heads sharing a cache head compete for a shared retrieval budget, and adaptively splits and merges retrieval resolution. Tested on long-form speech recognition, translation, and summarization across four speech language models, C3 gives the best overall results among retrieval methods at comparable access budgets, with especially large gains under tight budgets. It also improves long-context decoding efficiency and memory scaling.

entry.title: Déjà Vu: Cycle-Consistent Re-ranking for Matching Semantic Keypoints
entry.summary: Déjà Vu: Cycle-Consistent Re-ranking for Semantic Correspondence arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Déjà Vu, a test-time decoding module that improves semantic correspondence, the task of matching equivalent keypoints across images of the same object category. The authors observe that correct matches often appear among top-ranked candidates even when greedy top-1 selection misses them, and they frame matching as a recall-then-rerank problem. The method selects an adaptive candidate set and re-ranks it using a graded cycle-consistency score computed from the existing similarity matrix. It improves three baselines on SPair-71k, its geometric subset, and PF-Pascal under unsupervised and weakly supervised settings.

entry.title: Testing whether audio-language models trust what they hear or what they're told in the same recording
entry.summary: One Waveform, Two Stories: Benchmarking Speech-Acoustic Conflict in Audio-Language Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces SAC-Bench, a benchmark of 616,031 audio clips covering 188 sound-event classes across seven semantic, temporal, and spatial tasks. Each recording is paired with spoken claims that either match or contradict the acoustic content. Across five open-weight audio-language models, accuracy on event identity drops by 24.8 to 46.5 percentage points under conflicting claims. The authors also find that prompt interventions can restore acoustic accuracy in some cases but can also reduce claim-aligned answers without improving grounding.

entry.title: GAVAGAI: Aligning Words to Image Regions in Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport
entry.summary: GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes an alignment objective that links words to image regions in vision-language models by treating each scene as an assignment problem solved with entropic optimal transport. Words may be assigned to a NOTHING option instead of any region, and each region's share of assignment mass is capped.
