On the SAYCam infant video corpus, adding this alignment loss to a captioning model raised word-to-picture accuracy from 32.4% to 48.7% and localization IoU from 0.18 to 0.38. A contrastive model trained on the same child's data still performs better on its own benchmark.

entry.title: Overview of cyber-physical attack detection in wide-area measurement systems
entry.summary: Cyber-physical attack detection approaches in the wide-area measurement system arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines wide-area measurement systems (WAMS) in the Smart Grid, which use phasor measurement units (PMUs) to collect time-stamped data on voltage, current, frequency, and phase angle. It surveys cyber and physical anomalies in WAMS and their effects on system integrity and availability. The paper reviews anomaly detection approaches for historical and streaming PMU data, including conventional machine learning and hybrid methods, and discusses their strengths and drawbacks. It also highlights the importance of handling missing data and concept drift.

entry.title: Decentralized Coordination for Multiple Coding Agents in Shared Codebases (Paper)
entry.summary: Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication in Shared Codebases arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines how coding agents working in one shared repository, each serving a separate developer, can produce conflicting code when their changes are combined. The authors introduce ParallACT, a benchmark of complementary and contradictory coding tasks without an orchestrator. Parallel agents perform substantially worse than a single-agent oracle, with the sharpest drop on contradictory tasks. Telling agents about peers helps little, and a communication channel recovers only a small part of performance at extra token cost.

entry.title: RaMMOBO: A Fast Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization Method
entry.summary: RaMMOBO: Random Max-Margin Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces RaMMOBO, a multi-objective Bayesian optimization method for approximating the Pareto set of several expensive black-box objectives. Its acquisition function lower-bounds expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) while needing only linear cost in the number of objectives. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show it matches or outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with the largest gains at higher objective counts. Acquisition optimization is reported to be up to two orders of magnitude faster than qLogNEHVI.

entry.title: Low-precision floating point formats rising with deep learning and their standardization
entry.summary: The Rise of Low Precision Floating Point arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Floating point arithmetic has long dominated scientific computing because it balances precision and numerical range. Since 1985, 32-bit and 64-bit formats have been the industry standards. Over the past decade, deep learning has become the dominant workload, and narrower formats with lower precision and range have grown more common. The article discusses why this shift is happening, how 16-bit, 8-bit and 4-bit formats were developed, and efforts to standardize them.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Persona Effects in LLM Negotiation: Whether the Same Instruction Changes Negotiation Behavior in English and Korean
entry.summary: Cross-Lingual Persona Effects in LLM Negotiation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper has identical Gemini 3.6 Flash buyer and seller agents negotiate 12 CraigslistBargain scenarios in English and Korean, crossing seller urgency with three buyer personas across 432 attempted negotiations. Korean negotiations reached agreement far more often than English (77.3% vs. 52.5%), mainly with neutral and headstrong buyers, and sellers conceded more in Korean. The authors argue that changing only the interaction language can make a prompt-defined social policy produce different simulated negotiation behavior.

entry.title: A task-agnostic framework for counterfactual fairness in transformers using activation steering
entry.summary: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes MICF, a framework that uses mechanistic interpretability tools to reformulate counterfactual fairness constraints in terms of transformer activations. It unifies previous approaches into a single pipeline for fairness analysis, without requiring a prior causal model or a specific transformer architecture. The authors evaluate MICF on real-world tabular data and report that counterfactual fairness improves across different prediction tasks.

entry.title: Teach, Abstract, Apply: Teaching cobots new tasks through dialogue
entry.summary: Teach, Abstract, Apply: A Framework for Dialogue-Driven Task Learning with Collaborative Robots arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents the Teach-Abstract-Apply (TAA) framework, which lets human operators teach collaborative robots new workflows in natural language, abstract them into reusable skills, and apply those skills in different settings. The authors test the framework on a collaborative structure-building task using the open-weight Qwen3-Coder and the closed GPT5.2-Codex models in self-play and cross-model setups. Skill abstraction improved task success rates and reduced interaction cost. A preliminary human-in-the-loop study suggests the pipeline also works with human instructions.

entry.title: Seeing the Unseen: Unified Visible–Invisible Motion for Physically Consistent Video Generation
entry.summary: Seeing the Unseen: Unified Visible--Invisible Motion for Physically Consistent Video Generation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents Seeing the Unseen, a unified framework for generating videos that follow physical dynamics. It first uses a lightweight Particle-based Graph Dynamics Simulator (PGDS) to learn physical interactions from data and predict 3D motion trajectories. It then introduces a Visible–Invisible Motion Field (VIMF) that represents both motion visible in the input frame and motion emerging over time, and feeds these trajectories into a diffusion-based generator. The authors report improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency, and fewer physical artifacts than strong baselines.

entry.title: TADA: A Memory-Technology-Aware Estimator for DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy
entry.summary: TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents TADA, a estimator that predicts latency and energy of deep neural network accelerators for a given workload, hardware configuration, and memory technology. It is trained on a synthetic dataset spanning memory technologies, using technology signatures of read energy, write energy, and capacity as inputs. On 21 unseen technology curves, it achieves 1.5–4.4% mean absolute percentage error for energy and 0.7–1.2% for latency. It also reports evaluation throughput over 10^4 times higher than the simulator.

entry.title: Taxonomy of failures when AI agents act for users
entry.summary: When AI Agents Act on Our Behalf: A Taxonomy of Human-Agent Interaction Failure arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines how AI agents that write code, manipulate user interfaces, and make transactions for users can fail. The authors analyze 695 documented incidents from two public repositories and derive 12 failure modes across three interaction stages, coding the autonomy level at which each arose. They find that all 12 modes appear at both low and high autonomy, and that increasing autonomy changes the form each failure takes.

entry.title: Locating Photos from Narrow Views: Cross-View Geolocalization Using a Global Dataset
entry.summary: Seeing Less in a Sparse World: Cross-View Geolocalization from Limited Field-of-View Observations arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies cross-view geolocalization, which finds a ground photo's location by retrieving the matching satellite image, useful where GNSS signals are unavailable. The authors introduce CVW500k, a globally distributed dataset of over 500,000 ground-satellite image pairs that uses limited field-of-view ground images, closer to real cameras. They also propose GeoQueryNet, a query-based cross-view fusion transformer that uses a CLIP-based encoder with LoRA adaptation and learnable query tokens to align features across the two viewpoints.

entry.title: VerusWeave: A Benchmark for Repairing Proofs in Concurrent Verus Programs
entry.summary: VerusWeave: A Benchmark for Proof Repair in Concurrent Verus Programs arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces VerusWeave, the first benchmark dedicated to repairing proofs for concurrent code written in Verus, drawn from four open-source projects. It contains 75 focused tasks and 17 full-module variants, where selected proof annotations are removed and coding agents must fill the gaps while executable code and specifications are kept intact. An initial evaluation of four general-purpose coding-agent harnesses reached 75–85% success on focused tasks and 29–47% on full-module variants.

entry.title: A method for quantizing large models that handles weight outliers and sparsity
entry.summary: Quantization of Large Models with Weight Outliers and Sparsity arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Post-training quantization reduces the memory needed to deploy large models by storing their weights in fewer bits, but this causes errors that hurt performance. The paper splits the trained weights into a quantized matrix, a low-rank component, and a sparse matrix that captures outlier rows, using simulated annealing to search for good decompositions. Tests on Llama 3.2 1B and 3B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen2.5 7B with 4-bit NF4 and FP4 quantizers show it can clearly outperform direct quantization with minimal extra memory.

entry.title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Embeddings
entry.summary: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents OCELOT, a model that predicts where species occur across the globe by fusing spatial coordinates with satellite foundation embeddings. It is trained on about 2 billion GBIF records covering 100,000 taxa. On spatial holdouts testing extrapolation to remote areas, satellite embeddings improve performance by 51% over coordinate-only models and outperform classical bioclimatic rasters. The model also matches or exceeds existing baselines on interpolation benchmarks.

entry.title: DELBERT-2: Pretrained Fingerprint Language Models for DEL Protein Binder Prediction
entry.summary: DELBERT-2: Pretrained Fingerprint Language Models for DEL Protein Binder Prediction arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents DELBERT-2, a pretrained language model that converts sparse molecular fingerprints into token sequences using a ModernBERT encoder. It is trained with masked language modelling on 2.5 million molecules from the AIRCHECK DEL corpus. The model is evaluated on six targets under three out-of-distribution protocols, where it improves PR-AUC and NDCG@1000 over LightGBM baselines and transformers trained from scratch. The largest gains appear in the most stringent out-of-distribution settings.

entry.title: Constructive Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic
entry.summary: Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic by Construction from Triangular Standard Contradictions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a constructive framework for generating theorems automatically in first-order logic, built from minimally unsatisfiable clause sets formed from selected literals. Some clauses serve as premises and the negation of a clause or conjunction of clauses as the conclusion, so generated theorems are correct by construction without separate proofs. The authors extend their earlier Δ1 generator with methods Δ2 to Δ8, implementing and releasing Δ1 to Δ4, and present a general Δ-class method. Combinatorial analysis indicates that the approach can systematically produce large numbers of distinct theorems.

entry.title: Outstrumental Variable Regression: Identifying Causal Effects Using Outcome Mechanism Shifts Across Environments
entry.summary: Outstrumental Variable Regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Outstrumental Variable Regression (OVR), a method for estimating the causal effect of a treatment on an outcome from observational data when unobserved confounding is present. It shows the effect can be identified when the outcome mechanism varies across a finite set of environments, even if the treatment distribution is unchanged. The procedure computes conditional expectations per environment, forms a contrast vector against a reference environment, and regresses the outcome on the treatment while adjusting for the contrast and environment. The authors prove conditions under which OVR recovers the true effect, show a finite-sample version is consistent under regularity conditions, and demonstrate it on synthetic and real-world data.

entry.title: KINDER: A kernel-based method for fair representation learning by erasing sensitive information in prototype space
entry.summary: KINDER: Kernel-based Independence for Fair Representation Learning via Prototype-space Erasure arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces KINDER, a method that directly removes sensitive-attribute information from the intermediate representations of deep models. It operates in a random Fourier feature space, estimating a sensitive subspace from protected-group prototypes and projecting representations onto its orthogonal complement. The authors state the method works with any model containing an intermediate feature space and report experiments across supervised and self-supervised settings, multiple tasks, and visual, textual, and tabular data.

entry.title: SketchForge: training-free method turning images into editable vector sketches
entry.summary: SketchForge: Training-Free Scene-to-Vector Sketching via Decoupled Structure and Texture Optimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026SketchForge is a framework that converts a raster image into a resolution-independent, stroke-editable SVG sketch without any additional training or fine-tuning. It optimizes Bezier curves for each input image at test time, separating structural contour strokes from free-form texture strokes and compositing them via multiply-blend layering. The paper reports that it outperforms existing vector-based baselines in structural fidelity and generation quality.

entry.title: Taurus: LLM-in-the-loop CT annotation matching coding agents at half the cost
entry.summary: Taurus: LLM-in-the-Loop CT Annotation Matches Coding Agents at Half the Cost arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The authors present Taurus, a framework in which an automated pass labels aortic CT scans and a large language model reviews the result. They evaluated it by blind label recovery on six public datasets (939 volumes), scoring each approach against each dataset's own classes. The final version smooths label surfaces with a fixed rule and asks the model multiple-choice questions when automated checks flag large errors. It showed no difference from a free-form Opus agent on the primary metric, at $1.22 per case against $2.71.

entry.title: SketchBloom: Training-free vector sketch outpainting with stroke-level style control
entry.summary: SketchBloom: Training-Free Vector Sketch Outpainting with Stroke-Level Style Control arXiv · Oct 31, 2026SketchBloom is a training-free framework that extends sparse sketches and outputs an editable SVG made of Bezier strokes. It combines pretrained raster outpainting and style-transfer guidance with per-instance vector optimization to keep contours coherent and match a reference style. On LineArtOut-1K, with 1,024 input and style combinations, it reports better perceptual, semantic, and structural fidelity than the evaluated vector baselines. Runtime is about six minutes per pair on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU.

entry.title: MEMENTO: Learning to Manage Context for Long-Input Agents
entry.summary: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B that manages its fixed context window by compacting its history into self-written notes. It is first trained on synthetic trajectories with hindsight-generated notes, then refined with reinforcement learning using a reward covering answer correctness, note quality, and confidence calibration. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, it raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context.

entry.title: OmniPiano: A benchmark for dexterous robotic piano playing under standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent reinforcement learning.
entry.summary: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces OmniPiano, a benchmark for dexterous robotic piano playing that supports one to five Shadow Hands. It covers standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent reinforcement learning within a shared task family, with at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms. The benchmark also includes LLM-based agents, and experiments show that current state-of-the-art methods still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks.

entry.title: RE-SciVQA: Better Answers About Scientific Figures Using Relevant Retrieval and Light Model Tuning
entry.summary: RE-SciVQA: Improving Scientific VQA With Context-Relevant Retrieval and Lightweight MLLM Adaptation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents RE-SciVQA, a method for answering questions about figures in scientific papers. It expands queries with relevant section headers and adjusts retrieval scores using figure references and caption alignment, while fine-tuning small language models with LoRA. On the SciVQA benchmark it reaches a ROUGE-1 F1 of 73.9%, ahead of chart-focused models such as UniChart, ChartGemma and Matcha-ChartQA. Compared with a standard RAG baseline, it improves exact match by 11.9% and fuzzy match by 29.5%.

entry.title: IsoAlign: Isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment using joint-embedding predictive architectures
entry.summary: IsoAlign: Isoform-Aware DNA-Protein Alignment via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces IsoAlign, a multimodal framework for pretraining genomic foundation models by aligning transcripts with their corresponding protein isoforms to learn DNA representations. It uses two Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures: DP-JEPA, which predicts protein representations from DNA via contrastive alignment, and IM-JEPA, which models relationships among alternative isoforms of the same gene through masked protein prediction. The learned representations were evaluated on tasks including pathogenicity, fitness, gene expression, and TF binding prediction, and the authors report improved downstream performance from isoform-aware cross-modal alignment.

entry.title: Real-time source-free polyp segmentation using directional dual-head supervision
entry.summary: Directional Dual-Head Supervision for Real-Time Source-Free Polyp Segmentation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents MedRT-SFSeg, a real-time source-free domain adaptation framework for polyp segmentation built on a dual-head YOLO architecture. It introduces Mask-DHF to fuse precision- and recall-oriented predictions, DURR to use dual-head disagreement as a directional cue for adjusting masks and recovering missed instances, and Seg-MARD for mask-guided, region-stratified feature regularization. In bidirectional adaptation experiments between Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB, the method reports Dice scores of 80.43% and 80.77%, improving on the non-adapted baseline while running at over 62 FPS end-to-end.

entry.title: ProLand: a new optimizer for efficient LoRA fine-tuning of language models
entry.summary: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces ProLand, a retraction-free optimizer for LoRA fine-tuning that keeps low-rank factors near the Stiefel manifold. It combines coordinated factor updates with Muon-style spectral directions, separating objective optimization from orthogonality restoration. Experiments cover four GLUE tasks on DeBERTa-v3-base and seven language benchmarks on Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Moonlight-16B-A3B across several adapter ranks. The authors report that ProLand achieves the highest average score among compared methods in every tested model-rank configuration.

entry.title: Localized anomaly detection using a calorimeter normalizing flow
entry.summary: Localized anomaly detection with a calorimeter normalizing flow arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper uses a normalizing flow trained as a fast calorimeter simulator to compute each shower's likelihood, which serves as an anomaly score. Because the global likelihood sums over all voxels, a signal confined to a few voxels can be lost in the rest of the shower's fluctuations. The authors define a regional score by summing the squared latent coordinates of the same flow within small detector regions around where the particle enters the calorimeter. At the same background efficiency, this regional score selects more than 95% of the signal, compared with less than 5% for the global CaloFlow likelihood used in prior work.

entry.title: Spectral and Conformal: Neural Network Methods for Calibrated Trajectory Prediction and Control-Point Intervals
entry.summary: Spectral and Conformal: Neural Network Methods for Calibrated Trajectory Prediction and Control-Point Intervals arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents a framework for quickly assessing the feasibility and safety of trajectories for autonomous systems. It combines a spectral-backbone neural network that learns trajectories and quantile bands with built-in constraints, a modified conformal quantile regression for calibrated joint trajectory coverage, and interval arithmetic to extend noise-free coverage guarantees to control points. On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, quadrotor trajectory inference under a closed-loop LQR takes 3.45 ms, and the full pipeline takes 9.81 ms, or about 100 Hz.

entry.title: Editing Cell Nucleus Images Across Gene and Pathomics Data in Spatial Transcriptomics
entry.summary: From Cross-Section to Cross-Omics: Conditional Cell Nucleus Image Editing in Spatial Transcriptomics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper examines how tissue sectioning geometry creates an apparent correlation between gene expression and nuclear pathomics features in spatial transcriptomics. The authors apply the Manifold-Aware Diffusion (MAD) framework to condition-driven editing of cell nucleus images, modifying one feature group while preserving the other. Evaluated on podocyte cells from CosMx SMI kidney tissue, MAD achieves MAE 0.6636 and FID 25.19 for pathomics editing, outperforming all compared baselines.

entry.title: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Video Calls
entry.summary: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Communication arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces VC-1K, an open-source test set of about 1,000 video sequences for evaluating video processing and encoding in real-time communication. The videos are user-generated video call content recorded on consumer mobile devices under varied conditions, mostly talking-head footage with a small set of rear-camera videos without faces, and each includes synchronized audio. The authors evaluate OpenH264, SVT-AV1, and libaom under constant bitrate encoding, along with RealESRGAN and GFPGAN super-resolution methods.

entry.title: MemU-Bench: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Handling Vague, History-Dependent Long-Horizon Tasks
entry.summary: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces MemU-Bench, a mobile benchmark of 118 vague tasks built on 29 long-horizon user interaction trajectories, where agents must recall missing context from history. Task outcomes are verified against application databases, and metrics such as Interaction Efficiency and SPL are used to distinguish genuine recall from exhaustive search. The authors also propose AppMem, a training-free framework that builds a structured, app-centric memory bank, raising GPT-5.5's SPL from 15.7% to 66.9%.

entry.title: CAPER: Circuit-aware fine-tuning for LLM-based analog circuit verification
entry.summary: CAPER: Circuit-Aware Parameter-Efficient Reasoning in LLMs for Analog Verification arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes using large language models as assistants to verify analog circuits, flagging unmet specifications and reliability issues under process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variation. It introduces CAPER, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that adds a branch beside LoRA to read each circuit stage's properties and combine them across relevant stages. The authors report that CAPER correctly judges whether a feedback loop is negative and learns to flag PVT-induced failures in comparator latches, where generic adapters perform near chance.

entry.title: "Neurons Are All You Need": a new neural layer that stores persistent memory within units so learned abilities can transfer between model instances
entry.summary: Neurons Are All You Need arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes NURESA (Neural Unit with Retentive Self-Adaptive Architecture), a neural layer that adds persistent memory inside each unit, separate from computation, which accumulates and consolidates into transferable memory registers. Experiments on MLP, GPT-2 and Qwen2.5 report zero-shot transfer of learned capability into a naive model instance without retraining or the original training data. The authors also report that the method protects against domain loss during fine-tuning, and that transfer takes about one minute with files far smaller than the original model.

entry.title: Does vendor image processing matter? Learning how echocardiography displays look from raw beamspace data.
entry.summary: Does Vendor Image Processing Matter? Learning Echocardiography Display Appearance from Native Beamspace Data arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Many echocardiography datasets contain images processed by vendors, but that processing is often undocumented and may affect model performance and robustness. The researchers trained a small convolutional neural network to reproduce General Electric display appearance from native beamspace brightness-mode ultrasound, using 8,406 recordings from 605 patients. The beamspace CNN cut test mean absolute error by 43% relative to the optimal pointwise brightness map, outperformed an equivalent Cartesian CNN, and runs in real time on a CPU.

entry.title: Rate-distortion optimized skip mode coding for AVS neural video compression
entry.summary: A Rate-Distortion Optimized Skip Mode Coding Framework for Neural Video Compression in AVS arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies skip mode coding in neural video compression under the AVS standard, examining how rate and distortion are distributed across spatial positions and temporal reference qualities. It proposes RDOSkip, a framework that models skip-mode rate and distortion using statistical distributions predicted by a hyperprior and Bayes' theorem, with an adaptive decision method based on joint spatial-temporal rate-distortion optimization. The method requires no training, adds negligible complexity, and yields BD-rate savings of 0.90% on AVS and 1.29% on HEVC datasets.

entry.title: "Learning to Live": A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
entry.summary: Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces LIFE, a framework that lets robots observe continuously, remember selectively, and turn experience into new capabilities. It combines RoboBeats, lightweight streaming gates that track conditions and discover events; Plastic Memory, a flat store of images and structured records; and Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM), which turns validated problem-solving solutions into reusable tools and skills. Under matched protocols, RoboBeats improves condition tracking over its base models and retains more useful evidence than uniform sampling at the same writing budget. A limited case study replaying 24 hours of real-robot video shows the system building memory from a day of experience and answering everyday questions.

entry.title: How to Simplify a Line Chart: A Taxonomy and Feature-Based Evaluation
entry.summary: How to Simplify a Line Chart: A Taxonomy and Feature-Based Evaluation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a taxonomy for simplifying line charts based on how methods preserve visual features such as trends and extrema. It evaluates 19 algorithms across three families (Transformers, Reducers, and Aggregators) using 12 defined features and 21 preservation measurements. A Feature–Complexity score balances fidelity and simplicity, and results across 80 datasets show clear differences between algorithm families.

entry.title: AuroraWorld: 4D world modeling for generating robot-view videos from external cameras
entry.summary: AuroraWorld: Structured 4D World Modeling for Exo-to-Ego Video Generation in Robot Manipulation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026AuroraWorld is a method for synthesizing egocentric, robot-centric videos from large-scale exocentric manipulation videos, offering an alternative to costly egocentric data collection. The paper notes that existing approaches struggle to produce physically consistent, policy-relevant egocentric videos under large viewpoint changes, severe occlusions, complex object interactions, and sparse exocentric observations.

entry.title: Interpretable temperature scaling to calibrate graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation
entry.summary: Interpretable structural temperature scaling for calibrating graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Interpretable Structural Temperature Scaling (ISTS), a twelve-parameter linear model that sets each node's temperature from named descriptors of confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes. Each temperature can therefore be traced back to the contributions of these descriptors. Across seven graphs with two backbones, ISTS achieves the best average rank in negative log-likelihood and Brier score, lowering NLL by 1.8% relative to temperature scaling. On point-cloud segmentation, the authors report significant improvements in NLL, Brier score and point ranking for rejection.

entry.title: From fragmented embedding research to unified multimodal embeddings: a survey and roadmap
entry.summary: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper surveys omnimodal embeddings, the vector representations used across many data types. The authors argue that embedding research, split by modality, is converging on shared principles driven by contrastive learning, Transformers, and a shift in granularity. They propose three capabilities, coverage, comparability, and compositionality, and three paths toward unification: transformation, alignment, and joint embedding. It presents the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of this research.

entry.title: A survey of large language model methods for turning plain-language questions into database queries
entry.summary: Reimagining Text-to-SQL: A Survey of Large Language Model Architectures and Strategies arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Text-to-SQL systems convert natural language questions into executable SQL queries so people can access relational data more easily. This survey reviews large language model approaches within a taxonomy of five paradigms: in-context learning, supervised and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, agentic and tool-augmented orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and reinforcement learning. It also covers evaluation metrics, datasets, open challenges such as domain generalization, efficiency and deployment, and responsible AI practices for sensitive databases.

entry.title: PatchScout: Collecting Topic-Based Web Data by Information Foraging
entry.summary: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper addresses the need for collections of documents on a shared theme that are spread across many unconnected websites. It frames this as a long-horizon information foraging problem and proposes PatchScout, a multi-agent framework that balances exploring within a region against switching to new ones under a fixed budget. In experiments on four live-web topics, it improved yield and domain coverage over traversal-based and search-augmented reasoning agent baselines. In a social science application with an incomplete prior collection, it discovered 102 previously unidentified entities.

entry.title: Early stopping in reasoning models: a survey and audit of efficiency and reliability
entry.summary: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper surveys early-stopping methods for large reasoning models, which halt generation once enough reasoning exists to answer, reducing unnecessary computation. The authors evaluate several methods across five reasoning models on math and science reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks using a shared rollout replay protocol. They introduce Target-Integrated Token Efficiency (TITE) to measure efficiency relative to an oracle. The study reports that correctness can drop at later exit positions and that reasoning sometimes continues after forced termination.

entry.title: Learning to Bid and Bundle: A Posterior-Sampling Agent for Online Retail
entry.summary: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how an online retailer selling a perishable product can learn its bidding and discounting strategy over repeated seasons without knowing how clicks respond to bids or how strong its market is. The authors design a posterior-sampling agent that each period draws a market from the exact posterior and applies the exactly solved season plan for that market. In a simulated online florist, the method has the lowest regret averaged over markets, and in weak markets it loses 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons.

entry.title: A clustering method that automatically estimates the number of clusters
entry.summary: A Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering Framework with Automated Cluster Cardinality Estimation Ability arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering (GSFC), which adds a continuous sparsity penalty to the fuzzy clustering objective so that membership values can be exactly zero. It solves the problem with a primal-dual bisection search and can prune redundant clusters when initialized with more clusters than the true number. A virtual noise sink isolates outliers, and the framework is extended to line segment detection. Experiments report better results than conventional fuzzy methods and existing sparse soft-clustering methods on line detection.

entry.title: FlowFPR: A Flow Matching Prior Method for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
entry.summary: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes FlowFPR, a method for reconstructing images from Fourier magnitude measurements without phase information. It combines a pretrained Flow Matching prior with relaxed averaged alternating reflections, adding adaptive fusion and a controlled inner search with early stopping. Experiments on natural face images show the joint variant achieves the best mean quality at two nonzero noise levels, with lower end-to-end runtime than diffusion-based baselines.

entry.title: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models
entry.summary: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Toward Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This position paper argues that identifying the actual cause of a robot foundation model failure requires more than knowing which concepts the model has learned. The authors formalize fault isolation within the framework of actual causality and identify shortcomings in current mechanistic interpretability methods, such as assuming fixed contingencies and reading out only immediate effects. A toy example shows these shortcomings can produce conflicting verdicts. The paper concludes by outlining four open research tasks.

entry.title: Explainable multiple-instance learning of kidney biopsy features for kidney function classification
entry.summary: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study examines whether analyzing individual glomeruli with multiple-instance learning can add information beyond standard glomerular subtype ratios for classifying estimated glomerular filtration rate. It analyzes 162 kidney-biopsy whole-slide images, sorting patients by eGFR below or at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Combining pathomic features with subtype ratios gave the highest mean AUC, 0.7630 ± 0.0665, and SHAP was used to examine individual feature contributions.

entry.title: Contrastive Astromer: Two-Stage Contrastive Learning for Classifying Astronomical Light Curves
entry.summary: Contrastive Astromer: Two-Stage Contrastive Representation Learning for Astronomical Light Curve Classification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Contrastive Astromer, a two-stage method that improves representations of astronomical light curves for classification without changing the ASTROMER 2 encoder. It first applies unsupervised contrastive learning to MACHO light curves, then uses supervised contrastive learning with an auxiliary classification loss on labeled Alcock data. With the encoder frozen, a separate classifier trained with 500 labeled examples per class reaches a macro-F1 of 0.7943 on 600 held-out objects, 5.10 points above the reproduced ASTROMER 2 baseline.

entry.title: Toward Contrast-Free Breast MRI: Virtual Contrast Imaging to Improve Cancer Detection
entry.summary: Toward Contrast-Free Breast MRI: Improving Cancer Detection With Virtual Contrast Enhanced Imaging arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study addresses the need for intravenous gadolinium in contrast-enhanced breast MRI by combining predictions from non-contrast MRI with AI-generated virtual contrast-enhanced (VCE) MRI for cancer detection. On a held-out test set, non-contrast MRI alone achieved an AUROC of 0.865, which rose to 0.901 when combined with VCE predictions. A simulation suggests diagnostic performance can be largely preserved while limiting acquired contrast-enhanced imaging to about 40% of patients, indicating potential for selective contrast use in breast cancer screening.

entry.title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Decision Processes
entry.summary: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems that involve both forward and backward dynamics, which standard MDPs cannot express. It develops a theoretical framework for their optimal solutions and proposes a general forward-backward step-wise template for adapting reinforcement learning algorithms. The resulting Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) algorithm is evaluated on mathematical finance and mobile resource management use cases, where it reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across several metrics.

entry.title: SPARQLcirc: Probabilistic Query Evaluation Using Provenance Circuits
entry.summary: SPARQLcirc: Probabilistic Query Evaluation with Provenance Circuits arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies exact probabilistic query evaluation for SPARQL over uncertain knowledge graphs accessed through SPARQL 1.1 endpoints. It proposes SPARQLcirc, which rewrites SPARQL queries into CONSTRUCT queries so that all answers share one Boolean provenance circuit, and computes each answer's exact probability by weighted model counting. Experiments on WatDiv, gMark, and Wikidata data with GraphDB, Fuseki, and Oxigraph show that its time relative to compiling per-answer provenance expressions decreases as the number of derivations grows.

entry.title: CDBM: A Complexity-Diversity Framework for Analyzing Building Shapes
entry.summary: CDBM: Complexity-Diversity Framework for Building Morphology Analysis arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces CDBM, a set of twelve interpretable descriptors for building massings modeled as vertical extrusions. The metrics capture how strongly geometric detail is expressed (complexity) and how unevenly it varies across elements (diversity). CDBM was computed for 482,241,306 OpenStreetMap buildings and compared with 3DBM and the LION shape latent across several tasks. The authors report that CDBM best separates generated from mapped massings and best matches human preference, while 3DBM performs better on the other tasks, and they state that CDBM complements existing indicators.

entry.title: DTP-OPSD: A reinforcement learning method that uses marked distractor videos to help locate events in video.
entry.summary: DTP-OPSD: Reinforcement Learning with Distractor-Aware Temporal-Privilege On-Policy Self-Distillation for Temporal Video Grounding arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper addresses temporal video grounding, where a model must find when a described event occurs in a video, a task that is hard when similar or opposite events repeat. It proposes DTP-OPSD, in which a teacher model views a privileged video marking the target and distractor segments, and provides dense token-level supervision to a student model even when standard GRPO gives no useful gradient. Using only 300 additional training examples, the method achieves the highest mIoU among compared open-source 8B models on three benchmarks and improves all 12 reported metrics over pure GRPO trained on the same data.

entry.title: Predicting cognition from multimodal brain MRI using staged pretraining on partially observed cohorts
entry.summary: Brain-Behavior Modeling from Multimodal MRI using Opportunistic Pretraining and Common-Cohort Adaptation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study uses baseline Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study data to predict fluid, crystallized, and total cognition from MRI. Separate neural models process structural/diffusion, resting-state, and task-based MRI, are pretrained on eligible modality cohorts, adapted to common cohorts, and fused with Ridge regression. Two-stage training and fusion yield modest gains over constituent and covariate-only models, with expanded pretraining driving most improvements. The authors suggest the approach may support MRI-informed cognitive phenotyping, pending external validation.

entry.title: Predicting Thinking Abilities from Brain Structure MRI Using Spatial Graph Learning
entry.summary: Predicting Cognitive Profiles from Structural MRI using Spatial Graph Representation Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a Spatial-Topological Graph Neural Network (ST-GNN) that predicts four cognitive phenotypes from structural brain MRI in large pediatric cohorts (N = 2,378 to 2,424). Regional brain morphometry is projected onto a standardized spatial graph, so information is passed only between neighboring regions. The authors report that ST-GNN outperforms linear baselines and topology-free deep models, and that sparse K-nearest-neighbor topology and global feature scaling work best. Integrated Gradients analysis highlights features such as cerebellar volume and superior frontal surface area.

entry.title: SpatialVec: A unified method for representing points, lines, and shapes on maps with boundary-focused sampling
entry.summary: SpatialVec: A Unified Representation Learning Framework for Geospatial Objects with Boundary-Aware Sampling arXiv · Oct 28, 2026SpatialVec is a spatial representation learning framework that adaptively samples geometry boundaries and their surrounding regions to capture fine-grained, topology-sensitive structures. It uses a transformer-based encoder-decoder trained through geometry reconstruction to produce compact, unified embeddings for points, polylines, and polygons. Evaluated on two real-world datasets, it better preserves complex polygonal topological relationships and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on downstream prediction and classification tasks.

entry.title: A new way to model curves and smooth their shapes for image repair
entry.summary: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a new formulation of the elastica model, which describes curves through Euler's elastica energy, using a binary representation of curves. It gives a simple curvature formula based on convolution with a radial kernel, requiring no derivatives, so the energy becomes a weighted total variation that generalizes the ROF model. The authors combine FFT with split Bregman iteration, equivalent to an augmented Lagrangian method, to build efficient algorithms. Numerical experiments on binary image inpainting demonstrate their effectiveness.

entry.title: Working backward from measured electron beams to laser-plasma settings
entry.summary: Inverse modelling of a laser-plasma accelerator arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the inverse problem of inferring laser-plasma accelerator settings (gas pressure, normalised vector potential, nitrogen concentration) from a measured electron beam. An ensemble of mixture density networks, trained on particle-in-cell simulations, outputs several candidate settings with probabilities. Predictions are accurate on average (R² = 0.91), but for about two-thirds of beams two competing solutions share nearly the same a₀²p₁. A second measurement at a different plasma density reduces the error on a₀ by a factor of 2.6.

entry.title: Mutual Distillation and Dynamic Model Merging for RGB-Event Representation Learning
entry.summary: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses fusing conventional frame cameras with event cameras. Existing methods convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, which limits how well event data is used. The authors propose mutual distillation across multiple event encoders, at both feature and logit levels, and then merge their model parameters with a dynamic hierarchical strategy into one unified RGB-event representation model. The paper reports significant performance improvements across multiple event-based datasets.

entry.title: A detector-integrated tracker that combines several cues to reduce identity switches for small, occluded drone-view vehicles
entry.summary: Detector-Integrated Multi-Cue Association for Occlusion-Aware UAV Multi-Object Tracking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses multi-object tracking of vehicles in drone imagery, where targets are small, visually similar, and often occluded, causing identity switches. The method attaches lightweight projection heads to the YOLOv8n detector's neck to extract appearance embeddings via ROIAlign, so detection and embedding run in one forward pass. Its association cost combines motion, IoU, and appearance distances, with weights chosen by ablation, plus low-score rescue and appearance-memory protection. On the UAVDT benchmark it reports MOTA 28.33, HOTA 31.16, and IDF1 38.18 at 82.59 FPS, and reduces identity switches by 58.4% compared with DeepSORT.

entry.title: A lightweight multi-scale encoder for classifying images from few examples
entry.summary: A Novel Lightweight Multi-Scale Branching Encoder for Few-Shot Image Classification arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper presents Sum12, a lightweight convolutional encoder that improves the embedding stage of Prototypical Networks for few-shot image classification. It uses seven parallel convolutional branches whose kernel sizes sum to 12, so local and broader spatial structures are captured in one multi-scale feature space. The encoder was evaluated on Omniglot, CIFAR-FS, FC100, and miniImageNet and compared with the original Prototypical Network encoder. Sum12 generally improved low-shot performance over the basic encoder while keeping the model compact.

entry.title: Pano2BIM: A geometry-constrained AI agent that builds as-built BIM models from a floor plan and one 360° photo
entry.summary: Pano2BIM: A Geometry-Constrained Vision-Language Agent for As-Built BIM Generation from a Floor Plan and a Single 360^circ Image arXiv · Oct 25, 2026This paper presents Pano2BIM, a vision-language model agent that generates approximate IFC4 building models at LOD 200 from a floor plan with known room dimensions and a single 360-degree photograph. The model identifies landmarks and furniture, while deterministic tools estimate camera pose and compute metric object positions. In a preliminary evaluation in one laboratory, the proposed Measure workflow achieved a higher mean furniture-footprint IoU (0.53) than a single-response baseline (0.44). The measurement stage took about 3.8 minutes and USD 1.63 per run, and the full workflow about 42 minutes and USD 11.

entry.title: OCRia-1 Technical Report: A 4B Vision-Language Model for Document Parsing
entry.summary: OCRia-1 Technical Report arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This report introduces OCRia-1, a 4-billion-parameter vision-language model for parsing documents, with strengths in preserving table structure, extracting chart data and retaining text formatting. Its mean ParseBench score across four evaluated dimensions is 0.87, compared with 0.75 for the next-best system. The model was trained on curated synthetic and real pages, using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The authors report decoding at about 4,700 tokens per second on a single B200 GPU.

entry.title: Rethinking Feature Perturbation for Single-Source Domain Generalization: Representation-Space Analysis and a Spectral Case Study
entry.summary: Rethinking Feature Perturbation for Single-Source Domain Generalization: A Representation-Space Analysis and Spectral Case Study arXiv · Oct 23, 2026The paper proposes four measurable descriptors that capture how feature perturbations change a model's representations, and uses them to compare existing perturbation methods on two object-detection settings with style and weather shifts. It also introduces Dual-Invariant Spectral Perturbation (DISP), a non-learned Fourier-phase method with explicit controls over phase magnitude, channel coupling, and frequency support. The authors report that DISP achieves strong out-of-domain performance in their experiments.

entry.title: Testing how team size and goal type shape collaboration in LLM group simulations
entry.summary: Evaluating Context Sensitivity of Collaboration Behavior in Multi Party Simulation Frameworks arXiv · Oct 22, 2026This paper examines how contextual factors such as team size and goal type affect collaboration behavior in multi-party simulations built on large language models. Using a controlled full-factorial study and established social science taxonomies, the authors quantify this context sensitivity. They report that simulated teams consistently favor smooth collaboration over disagreement, negotiation pressure, and coordination breakdown.

entry.title: AdaptAD: Foundation Model Adaptation Robust to Missing Data for Staging Alzheimer's Disease
entry.summary: AdaptAD: Foundation Model Adaptation with Missing Modality Robustness for Alzheimer's Disease Staging Across the Disease Continuum arXiv · Oct 19, 2026AdaptAD classifies Alzheimer's disease into cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia stages from a single T1-weighted structural MRI. It feeds 16 anatomically placed 2.5-D slices through the medial temporal lobe into a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 adapted with low-rank adaptation, and uses a learned [MISSING] token when FreeSurfer morphometry is unavailable. On the external OASIS-3 cohort it achieved a macro-AUC of 0.780, and removing morphometry changed external macro-AUC by less than 0.003. The authors report that the model stratifies MCI-to-dementia progression and that saliency focused on medial temporal and periventricular regions.

entry.title: HistGramBench: A benchmark for measuring how well multimodal models recover the structure of historical math diagrams redrawn as TikZ
entry.summary: HistGramBench: Measuring Structural Recovery When Multimodal Models Redraw Historical Mathematical Diagrams as TikZ arXiv · Oct 19, 2026Digital libraries hold historical math books whose diagrams are scanned images and cannot be searched. This paper introduces HistGramBench, containing 2,507 diagrams from 95 works printed between 1551 and 1933 in eight languages. Two AI models from different providers agree on the facts a reader takes from each figure, and every model's redrawing is checked against those facts. The best model recovers about three fifths of them, and most misses come from programs that never produce a drawing. Parallels and tangencies are the hardest relations to reproduce.

entry.title: Sequential Transfer Learning for Plant Disease Recognition Across Crops
entry.summary: Sequential Transfer Learning for Plant Disease Recognition Across Perennial Crop Domains Using MobileNetV2-CBAM arXiv · Oct 19, 2026This paper examines whether a lightweight MobileNetV2 model with CBAM attention can be reused step by step across different perennial crops. The model was transferred from walnut to cashew, coffee and mango, then tested on the mixed six-crop ABCGMP benchmark. Test accuracy rose from 75.76% on the walnut baseline to 84.85% with CBAM, then reached 90.67% on cashew, 100.00% on coffee and 99.50% on mango. On ABCGMP the model achieved 88.44% accuracy, 81.49% balanced accuracy and 0.9949 ROC-AUC. The study finds that substantial predictive ability was kept through successive transfers, while greater multi-crop diversity caused a measurable drop in performance.

entry.title: From Zero to OCR: A data-centric method for building text recognition for unsupported scripts.
entry.summary: From Zero to OCR: A Data-Centric Framework for Unsupported Low-Resource Scripts arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper proposes a framework that builds optical character recognition for low-resource scripts using only an unannotated text corpus and digital fonts, with no manually labeled training images. It is demonstrated on Kashmiri, a Nastaliq script that none of six widely used OCR engines supports. The resulting system reaches 10.0% character error rate on synthetic pages and 13.5% on browser-rendered digital pages. The authors release trained models, inference code, and a synthetic dataset of 285,864 Kashmiri text-line images.

entry.title: CRAFT: A Self-Correcting Multi-Agent Framework for Text-to-Parametric CAD
entry.summary: CRAFT: Corrective and Robust Multi-Agent Framework for Text-to-Parametric CAD arXiv · Oct 17, 2026CRAFT is a multi-agent framework that generates parametric OpenSCAD programs from natural language without task-specific training. Its core is a JSON intermediate representation that keeps symbolic parametric expressions throughout generation, so the models stay editable. It uses multi-view visual feedback to detect and repair geometric errors. On NopSCADlib, ABC, and Slice-100K, it is competitive with direct zero-shot baselines in perceptual and geometric quality while exposing more editable parametric structure.

entry.title: When Morphs Look Better: Face Image Quality as a Training-Free Morph Detection Signal
entry.summary: When Morphs Look Better: Face Image Quality as a Training-Free Signal for Morphing Attack Detection arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper evaluates 17 face image quality assessment methods by using each quality score directly as a morphing attack detection score. Tests cover 20 attack sets from the FRLL and FEI datasets, including five diffusion-based sets. Score directions were fixed in advance from each method's definition, so cases where morphs get higher quality than genuine samples remain visible. On FRLL, DifFIQA(R) achieved the lowest mean D-EER at 11.42%.

entry.title: When classification in the frequency domain outperforms the spatial domain
entry.summary: When frequency domain classification is superior to spatial arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This study finds that image classification models lose much accuracy in the frequency domain, mainly because they lack local features. Swapping data locally in the frequency domain shows this effect. Based on these results, the authors build a hybrid model that combines one model trained in the frequency domain and another trained in the spatial domain to raise accuracy. The VGG and ViT architectures are evaluated on six datasets.

entry.title: CRaFT-XDet: A Causal, Robust Transformer for Detecting Prohibited Items in Dual-Energy X-ray Scans
entry.summary: CRaFT-XDet: Causal and Robust Fusion Transformer for Dual-Energy X-ray Prohibited Item Detection arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper presents CRaFT-XDet, a method for detecting prohibited items in X-ray security images. It frames detection as learning representations that stay consistent across different scanners, combining causal feature disentanglement, physics-motivated regularisation, and transformer-based interaction between two energy channels. The authors report 0.9389 mAP@0.5 on SIXray and good performance on OPIXray and HiXray without domain adaptation, with real-time inference speed.

entry.title: How Reliable Object Detectors Are Outside Clear Weather: A Robustness Study for Self-Driving Cars
entry.summary: How Reliable Are Object Detection Models Beyond Clear Weather? A Deployment-Oriented Robustness Study for Autonomous Driving arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This study tests object detection models trained only on clear daytime driving scenes, without any adaptation, under unseen fog, rain, snow, and night conditions. It compares lightweight and medium-scale one-stage, two-stage, and transformer-based detectors using performance drop, a Weather Robustness Index, and calibration error. Performance degrades in all adverse conditions, reaching a 62.90% drop at night. YOLO-based detectors show the lowest calibration mismatch, while DETR has the lowest robustness score.

entry.title: SAMP: Self-Adaptive Margin Prioritization for Robust Diffusion Watermarking
entry.summary: SAMP: Self-Adaptive Margin Prioritization For Robust Diffusion Watermarking arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper presents SAMP, a framework for embedding watermarks in images generated by diffusion models. It adjusts embedding strength during denoising based on the separation between the target and competing codewords and the estimated effects of common attacks, and gives higher optimization priority to watermark dimensions that local perturbations can easily weaken. Experiments report an average information recovery accuracy of 0.993, with PSNR improved by 16.8% and LPIPS reduced by 47.1% compared with state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: MedICL: A Method for Improving Medical Visual Question Answering Without Retraining
entry.summary: MedICL: Modality-Anatomy-Aware Visual In-Context Learning for Medical Visual Question Answering arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper presents MedICL, a training-free approach that improves medical vision-language models by curating demonstration examples rather than retraining the model. It selects modality- and anatomy-aligned demonstrations, verifies them with a voting scheme, and aggregates answers using abnormality-aware signatures with re-answering on conflict. On VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA, it outperforms the strongest zero-shot baseline and remains robust to shifted or corrupted demonstration banks.

entry.title: Comparing single-camera and multi-camera methods for reconstructing 3D pedestrian motion at intersections
entry.summary: Comparing Monocular and Multi-View 3D Pedestrian Reconstruction Strategies for Urban Intersection Sensing arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper compares two methods for deriving pedestrian motion data, such as 3D body pose, metric trajectories, stature, and walking speed, from multi-camera footage of urban intersections. One is a monocular learned pipeline using text-prompted segmentation, tracking, and 3D body estimation; the other is a calibrated multi-view geometric pipeline using 2D pose estimation, cross-camera association, and triangulation. Since no 3D ground truth is available, the methods are assessed with reference-free criteria such as pedestrian coverage and anthropometric plausibility. The learned pipeline is easier to deploy and covers more pedestrians but suffers from scale ambiguity and height compression, while the geometric pipeline gives metric results more efficiently but needs calibration and discards single-camera detections.

entry.title: BreastXAgent: A lightweight agent framework that explains breast density classification
entry.summary: BreastXAgent: A lightweight agentic explainability framework for breast density classification arXiv · Oct 14, 2026This paper presents BreastXAgent, a lightweight agentic framework combining a pretrained classifier, Grad-CAM visual explanations, LangGraph-based routing, LLM report generation, and rule-based guardrails. It aims to produce controlled, faithful, non-diagnostic reports for breast density classification. Tested on 160 mammography images, uncontrolled LLM reports showed frequent overclaims, while the full framework reached a 100% safety pass rate with zero overclaims. The authors conclude that agentic guardrails enable safe, structured explanations without modifying the underlying classifier.

entry.title: OpenMidnight: Narrowing the Gap Between Open and Proprietary Pathology Models
entry.summary: OpenMidnight: Closing the Performance Gap Between Open and Proprietary Pathology Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 14, 2026This paper presents OpenMidnight 1.1, an open-source replication and refinement of the Midnight pathology foundation model. It is trained on about 12,000 public whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas and uses DINOv2-initialized weights, requiring about 320 H100 GPU-hours, a 34-fold reduction from Midnight's reported compute. On THUNDER's 16 classification and four segmentation datasets, it reaches the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models. The training code, preprocessing pipeline, and model weights are released.

entry.title: CarDiff: Anatomy-Aware Diffusion Model for Synthesizing Dental Caries Images
entry.summary: CarDiff: Anatomically Aware Dental Caries Synthesis using Diffusion arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper presents CarDiff, a semi-supervised diffusion framework that synthesizes dental caries in panoramic radiographs, using paired mask-image learning and anatomy-aware conditioning between lesions and surrounding structures. On the MLUA-DC1000 dataset, it achieves the best FID (90.76) and LPIPS (0.48) among evaluated methods. The generated images were also used to augment training data for seven segmentation architectures, improving average Dice score by up to 6.5% with a 5x augmented set.

entry.title: DDEL: Closed-Loop Mutual Enhancement of Dataset Distillation and Ensemble Learning
entry.summary: DDEL: Closed-Loop Mutual Enhancement of Dataset Distillation and Ensemble Learning arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper proposes DDEL, a framework that feeds ensemble learning behavior back into dataset distillation. Each round trains an ensemble, measures loss and prediction disagreement on source data, and uses these signals to update the distilled set. Preliminary experiments on ISIC 2019, I-SPY1 and NSCLC-Radiomics, at the same images-per-class budget, report balanced accuracy of 0.3471 on ISIC and mean ROC-AUC of 0.5120 and 0.5597 on I-SPY1 and NSCLC. The I-SPY1 gain is small, and more rounds do not consistently improve ISIC performance; computational cost and robustness remain to be evaluated.

entry.title: Memorix: A memory system that pre-selects what AI agents read
entry.summary: Memorix: Managing Memory Selections for AI Agents arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper proposes Memorix, a memory system for AI agents that computes which project materials an agent should read once in advance and reuses them across tasks. It relies on an immutable, versioned store, a View that separates selection from composition, and refreshable Quests and Profiles. On the SWE-ContextBench and LibEvolutionEval benchmarks, precomputed environments raised the resolved rate by up to 1.5X and delivered the correct library version on every version-conditioned task.

entry.title: Not All Minorities Are Equal: Privacy's Uneven Effects on Face Generation Fairness
entry.summary: Not All Minorities Are Equal: Fairness Outcomes in Private Image Generation arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper examines how differentially private training affects the representation of demographic groups and visual attributes in generative models of human faces. Using two facial image datasets across multiple privacy levels, it finds that stronger privacy can disproportionately degrade quality and utility for some underrepresented groups, potentially amplifying existing disparities. However, data representation alone does not explain these effects, as several well-represented attributes also degrade substantially.

entry.title: CausalPrune: Counterfactual causal pruning of visual tokens to speed up large vision-language models
entry.summary: CausalPrune: Counterfactual Causal Token Pruning for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 13, 2026Large vision-language models are slowed down by the many visual tokens they process. This paper proposes CausalPrune, which scores each visual token by its causal effect on the output using counterfactual analysis rather than correlation. It prunes tokens progressively across transformer layers using layer-wise causal mediation. Experiments on LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL report reduced FLOPs and prefill latency with comparable or better multimodal performance than existing pruning methods.

entry.title: SemaNorm: Stain normalization that preserves tissue shape and meaning for pathology images across hospitals
entry.summary: SemaNorm: Stain Normalization via Semantic and Morphology Alignment for Robust Cross-Hospital Computational Pathology arXiv · Oct 12, 2026SemaNorm is a self-supervised stain normalization method that recovers clean image patches from strongly perturbed inputs without paired data or adversarial training. It combines a frozen pathology foundation-model consistency loss with a differentiable nuclei-structure loss to preserve semantics and cellular organization. Evaluated on Camelyon17-WILDS and NCT-CRC-HE-100K, it improves out-of-distribution accuracy by 5.9% over the strongest normalization baseline and 13.5% over no normalization, with the best morphology preservation.

entry.title: From Clips to Streams: A Unified Framework for Real-Time Sign Language Translation
entry.summary: From Clips to Streams: A Unified Framework for Streaming Sign Language Translation arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper proposes StreamSLST, an end-to-end model that translates sign language from continuous, untrimmed videos rather than pre-cut clips. It uses a Deformable Transformer to jointly segment and translate in one pass, avoiding errors from cascaded pipelines. Experiments on BOBSL, How2Sign, and two new synthetic streaming benchmarks show it outperforms a matched segmentation-then-translation baseline.

entry.title: Auditing GeoFM Evaluation for Field-Extent Segmentation
entry.summary: Auditing GeoFM Evaluation for Field-Extent Segmentation: Label Proxies, Baselines, and When Frozen Features Match Fine-tuning arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper examines how label choices and baselines affect evaluations of geospatial foundation models for agricultural field-extent segmentation. Using single-date Sentinel-2 pixels from six countries, it shows that replacing polygon-derived field labels with ESA WorldCover cropland labels raises random-forest AUROC from 0.55-0.82 to 0.79-0.96. It also compares frozen and fully fine-tuned Prithvi and TerraMind models with matched seeds, finding frozen decoders often match fine-tuning, with Kenya as the main exception. The authors argue that labels and baselines should be audited before interpreting model rankings.

entry.title: SIMIT: Vision-language models improving themselves by imagining practice data at test time
entry.summary: SIMIT: Self-Improving Vision-Language Models via Imagination at Test-Time arXiv · Oct 12, 2026SIMIT is a framework in which a vision-language model generates its own question-specific training data before answering an unlabeled test query, without annotations or external models. The model specifies each answer first and then produces a matching image, creating (question, answer, image) triplets that pass multi-stage verification and difficulty filtering. This data can be used for in-context learning (SIMIT-ICL) or weight fine-tuning (SIMIT-FT). Across 17 benchmarks, SIMIT outperforms existing self-improvement methods, with its best configuration reaching a +7.20% mean relative gain over BAGEL-7B and training-free SIMIT-ICL reaching +6.98%.

entry.title: ReactionBench: A Human-Anchored Benchmark for Viewer Reactions to Video
entry.summary: ReactionBench: A Human-Anchored Benchmark for Modeling Reactions to Video arXiv · Oct 11, 2026This paper introduces ReactionBench, a benchmark for understanding viewers' reactions to videos. Built from 31,834 synchronized stimulus-reaction clips spanning 433 hours and eight domains, it tests ranking reaction intensity, matching a reaction to its aligned stimulus, and explaining the stimulus cues behind a reaction. Evaluating seven multimodal models, the authors find reaction-specific grounding remains difficult, with the best model reaching 50.9% accuracy on four-way matching.

entry.title: Assessing and Reducing Background Bias in Plant Disease Detection with EfficientNet-B0
entry.summary: Background Bias Assessment and Mitigation in Plant Disease Detection Using EfficientNet-B0 with Image Processing arXiv · Oct 11, 2026This paper examines whether deep learning models for plant disease detection rely on background cues rather than actual leaf disease features. The authors test an EfficientNet-B0 model under three conditions: original, leaf-only, and background-only images. On the PlantVillage dataset, accuracy was 98.97% on original images, 96.62% on leaf-only images, and 23.58% on background-only images, giving a background bias coefficient of 0.762.

entry.title: Keyframes First, Motion Second: Revisiting Video Captioning from Compressed Video Under Limited Data
entry.summary: Keyframes First, Motion Second: Revisiting Compressed-Domain Video Captioning under Limited Supervision arXiv · Oct 11, 2026The paper studies whether the motion branch of compressed-domain video captioners such as CoCap helps when training data is limited. In a controlled study on 2,500 VATEX training clips, motion encoders trained from scratch gave no significant CIDEr gain. Fine-tuning the keyframe encoder's attention-pooling head improved CIDEr by 5.4 while decoding only I-frames, which is faster. The authors conclude that under limited supervision, keyframes matter more than motion.

entry.title: TopoMix: Smooth Spatial Mixing for Long-Tailed Data Augmentation
entry.summary: TopoMix: Continuous Spatial Mixing for Long-Tailed Data Augmentation arXiv · Oct 10, 2026TopoMix is a training-free data augmentation method that replaces fixed mixing ratios with continuous spatial mixing. It builds a smooth, spatially varying mask from a low-resolution random grid, bicubic interpolation, and nonlinear shaping, then uses it for pixel-wise image mixing and label reweighting. Experiments on standard long-tailed benchmarks show consistent gains over representative mixing-based baselines.

entry.title: Circumpolar Mapping of Retrogressive Thaw Slumps Under Scarce Labels
entry.summary: Circumpolar Wall-to-Wall Detection of Retrogressive Thaw Slumps with Scarce Labels and Extreme Class Imbalance arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This paper presents a deep learning system that maps retrogressive thaw slumps (RTS), a type of permafrost ground collapse, across 20.68 million square kilometres of circumpolar permafrost using 4.8 m PlanetScope imagery. The authors treat RTS as a rare-target problem, comparing many model designs in 172 controlled experiments. The final model, tested at real-world prevalence, produced a circumpolar map of 19,068 high-confidence detections.

entry.title: SparseWAM: Efficient Driving World-Action Model Using 16 Register Tokens
entry.summary: SparseWAM: Driving World-Action Models are Worth 16 Register Tokens arXiv · Oct 9, 2026SparseWAM is a driving world-action model that jointly forecasts future scenes and ego trajectories within a sparse space of only 16 tokens per frame. These tokens are compressed from frozen DINOv2 features and shaped by joint planning-and-scoring pretraining. The model reaches 92.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 39.6 on NavHard, with a latency of 164 ms.

entry.title: Detecting AI-generated images from unseen generators using whitened noise residuals
entry.summary: Out-of-distribution AI-generated image detection with zero-phase deconvolution for residual whitening arXiv · Oct 8, 2026Current AI-generated image detectors often perform poorly on generators not included in their training data. This paper removes generator-specific fingerprints by applying a deconvolution step that whitens the spatial distribution of image noise residuals. An end-to-end CNN trained on these whitened residuals improves detection by 12.6% on average compared with training on original images.

entry.title: Diagnosing Zero-Shot Forgetting in CLIP Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Diagnosing Zero-Shot Forgetting in CLIP Fine-Tuning: Attention Drift Characterizes Adaptation, Representation Drift Predicts Transfer Degradation arXiv · Oct 8, 2026This paper examines whether the loss of CLIP's zero-shot accuracy after fine-tuning can be predicted from unlabeled target images. It compares four signals: CLS attention entropy, linear CKA with the pretrained model, embedding drift, and relative weight change. Experiments use ViT-B/32 and ViT-B/16 with full fine-tuning and LoRA on several datasets. The authors find CKA suited to comparing configurations, while attention entropy is informative only within a single configuration.

entry.title: Reasoning Before Localizing: Clinical Chain-of-Thought Supervision for Sequential Medical Image Grounding
entry.summary: Think Before You Locate: Clinical Chain-of-Though Supervision for Sequential Medical Image Grounding arXiv · Oct 8, 2026Vision-language models for sequential medical image grounding are usually trained only on bounding boxes, which show where a target is but not why that region answers the question. The authors build MedChain, a corpus of 182,573 filtered rationales across eight sequential grounding tasks and ten imaging modalities, and fine-tune Qwen3.5 with deliberative chain-of-thought supervision (dCoT-SFT). The 27B model reaches 77.24 mIoU and 85.20 Acc@0.5 on MedSG-Bench, with gains mainly in change detection and object tracking and drops on three appearance-matching tasks.

entry.title: Smartphone app that detects obstacles and estimates distance in real time for visually impaired and distracted pedestrians
entry.summary: Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Distance Estimation on Smartphones for Visually Impaired and Distracted Pedestrians arXiv · Oct 8, 2026This paper presents a Kotlin-based Android app that uses a YOLOv8 detector retrained to recognize eighteen urban obstacle classes to alert visually impaired users and distracted pedestrians in real time. Pruning, quantization, and early-exit branches, combined with NNAPI hardware acceleration, cut average inference latency on a mid-range phone from about 3.2 s to 0.39–0.48 s, with recall of 0.81 in the recommended configuration. The app needs only a single smartphone camera and provides text-to-speech and vibration feedback.

entry.title: Beyond Black Boxes: Transparent Ontology-Based Fruit Disease Detection
entry.summary: Beyond Black Boxes: An Ontology Based Vision Framework for Transparent Fruit Disease Detection arXiv · Oct 7, 2026This paper presents a hybrid framework combining real-time vision with a semantic knowledge base to detect fruit diseases without relying on large annotated datasets or opaque deep learning models. The authors built a fruit disease ontology in OWL that formally encodes phytopathological knowledge, including symptom, HSV spectral, and morphological phenotypes, to guide the image processing pipeline. On the public MangoFruitDDS dataset, the approach achieved an F1 score, precision, and recall of 85.00%, 85.00%, and 85.23%, respectively.

entry.title: Estimating tropical cyclone surface winds from satellite images using image-to-image AI
entry.summary: Tropical Cyclone Wind Field Diagnosis with Image-to-Image Models arXiv · Oct 7, 2026This study uses image-to-image generative adversarial networks to produce a full tropical cyclone surface wind field from a single satellite infrared image. Two models were trained, one on WRF simulations and one on real GOES images paired with parametric wind fields. Both models achieve mean RMSE values of 6.4 to 7.2 knots against held-out truth.

entry.title: Using Deep Learning to Detect Building Setback Violations in Dhaka
entry.summary: Deep Learning for Detecting Building Setback Rule Violations in Urban Planning: A Case Study on Bangladesh arXiv · Oct 7, 2026Rapid urban growth in Dhaka has made building setback violations common, narrowing footpaths and blocking emergency access. The study compares four machine learning methods for classifying setback conditions from street-level photos as compliant, borderline, or violating. On a 1,275-image test set, a fine-tuned ResNet18 CNN performed best at 65.4% accuracy, while all models struggled with the borderline class.

entry.title: From Single-Shot QA to Continuous Perception: Energy Composition of Edge VLMs
entry.summary: From Single-Shot QA to Continuous Perception: Revisiting the Energy Composition and Optimization Boundary of Edge VLMs arXiv · Oct 7, 2026This paper revisits energy conclusions for edge vision-language models under continuous perception rather than single-shot workloads. Profiling nine VLMs across three architecture families on Jetson AGX Thor and Orin (4,508 records), the authors find that visual-prefill energy reaches 92–97% of total energy under continuous perception with sparse output. They derive deployment strategies including visual frame reuse, adaptive output truncation, task-aware routing, and encoder throughput optimization.

entry.title: Noise-robust query retrieval for small-object detection via selective positional allocation (SPAR)
entry.summary: Selective Positional Allocation for Noise-Robust Query Retrieval in Small-Object Detection arXiv · Oct 7, 2026This paper presents SPAR, a detection framework that treats positional cues as a resource to allocate, strengthening them at meaningful locations and suppressing clutter-driven responses, for detecting tiny objects in aerial and remote-sensing imagery.
