It combines Selective Positional Embedding, an encoder called MOHFE, a decoder called HIDQ, and DPSConv for sparse small-object features. Across six datasets including DOTA and DIOR, SPAR improves over the baseline by up to 9.1 percentage points, reduces the decoder from eight to three layers, and cuts parameters by 59.4%.

entry.title: A trustworthy decision-support framework for classifying brain tumor MRI scans, combining attention, explainability, and out-of-distribution input screening.
entry.summary: A Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support Framework for Brain Tumor MRI Classification: Integrating Attention-Guided Learning, Explainable AI, and Out-of-Distribution Validation arXiv · Oct 7, 2026The paper presents a system that classifies brain MRI scans into glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, or no tumor, using an InceptionResNetV2 model with attention modules. Grad-CAM visualizations explain its predictions, and a two-stage check screens out unsuitable inputs. These parts are combined into a real-time web application called NeuroScan AI. On a dataset of 12,064 images, it reached 96.73% test accuracy and a macro-average AUC of 0.9965.

entry.title: Multimodal Cross-Condition Learning for Locating Video Moments from Sentences
entry.summary: Multimodal Cross-Condition Learning for Temporal Sentence Grounding in Videos arXiv · Oct 6, 2026This paper proposes Multimodal Cross-Condition Learning (MCCL), a method for temporal sentence grounding in videos, meaning finding the time segment that matches a text query. Its Video Prefix Adapter converts pooled visual context into tokens that condition a frozen DistilBERT encoder, and together with the Sentence Conditioned Adapter it enables an ordered exchange from vision to language and back. The authors test two video backbones and four conditioning modes on Charades-STA and ActivityNet Captions. On Charades-STA, bidirectional conditioning outperforms the stronger one-way mode by 1.6 to 2.3 mIoU points in all four settings.

entry.title: Gaussifier: A Fast Method for Decomposing Images into 2D Gaussians
entry.summary: Gaussifier: Fast 2D Gaussian Decomposition arXiv · Oct 6, 20262D Gaussian representations render images very quickly, but fitting each image takes seconds of optimization, which limits them to offline use. This paper presents Gaussifier, a lightweight feedforward framework that learns a density map of Gaussian centers and places them using equal-mass Voronoi partitioning. A reusable network then refines the result in a few iterations, reaching over 60 FPS.

entry.title: Estimating badminton shuttle speed from one camera using air drag and court geometry
entry.summary: Monocular Badminton Speed Estimation with Air Drag and Court Geometry arXiv · Oct 6, 2026This paper estimates badminton shuttlecock speed from a single smartphone camera. Court lines are used for calibration, and a gravity-and-drag trajectory is fitted to observed shuttle positions and frame timestamps. A fit constrained to cross the net plane is compared with a free fit. On 51 shots from two recording sessions, the net-plane fit reduced the median absolute speed difference from a drag-based stereo reference from 13.3% to 8.6%.

entry.title: DiA: Directional Adapter, a parameter-efficient method for fine-grained action recognition
entry.summary: DiA: Directional Adapter arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper addresses fine-grained action recognition, where temporal progression of an action matters more than appearance. It proposes DiA, a parameter-efficient adapter on top of CLIP that models causal and anti-causal temporal directions separately and fuses them with a learnable combination. Using only the video modality, DiA reportedly achieves state-of-the-art results among single-video-input methods on seven public benchmarks, with about 3.6M tunable parameters. It also reports higher throughput and lower inference latency than prior methods.

entry.title: Systematic Analysis of Live Surgeon Narration During Surgery
entry.summary: A Systematic Analysis of Live Intraoperative Surgical Expert Narrations arXiv · Oct 5, 2026Researchers analyzed live spoken commentary from 13 endoscopic lumbar spine decompression surgeries (13.2 hours) by two senior surgeons. An annotation-free pipeline converted speech into time-stamped procedural cues, retaining 37.9% of utterances, many referencing instruments, anatomy, and actions. Instrument requests preceded the instrument's appearance on screen by a median of 8.2 seconds, and 18.0% of retained cues had domain-term transcription errors.

entry.title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Fast, High-Quality Image Generation
entry.summary: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper introduces Scale-Free Attention (SFA), which keeps fine local interactions while summarizing distant regions at progressively coarser scales, giving O(N log N) complexity. Its Triton implementation reports about 357× forward and 266× backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens. After 40 epochs of PixelFlow training on ImageNet at 256×256, SFA achieves the best FID-50k among five attention mechanisms, improving from 13.25 for full attention to 12.51.

entry.title: "The Margin Knows the Background": Studying Uneven Abstention in Frozen Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: The Margin Knows the Background: Uneven Abstention in Frozen Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper studies how confidence scores in frozen vision-language models (OpenAI CLIP, LAION CLIP, SigLIP) can cause selective prediction to reject examples from some groups more often than others. The authors express margin and maximum-logit scores through the average and difference of the two highest class logits, and compare them against a randomized margin baseline. Experiments on Waterbirds and NICO++ show the effect of score choice depends on the dataset, and that how far a score pushes a group down its ranking tracks coverage gaps better than group identifiability alone.

entry.title: GazeRIB: A Systematic Test of Using Multiple Radiologists' Eye Gaze to Train Chest X-ray AI
entry.summary: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes GazeRIB, a method that trains medical imaging models by masking regions radiologists did not view, while using full images at inference. Eight experts read the same 80 chest X-rays, and reader panels of one, three, five, and eight were compared across architectures and seeds. Every panel improved macro F1 for four-class severity prediction on a separate cohort, while external validation results varied by dataset.

entry.title: Continuous-space latent reasoning for unified multimodal image generation (LARC)
entry.summary: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of unified multimodal models in using language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation, attributing it to a mismatch between discrete token reasoning and continuous image generation. It proposes LARC, which reasons over continuous hidden states through two stages: curriculum supervised fine-tuning that gradually shifts token-level reasoning to latent reasoning, and information-gain reinforcement learning that self-evolves without ground truth supervision. Experiments on text-to-image benchmarks report improved generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, with state-of-the-art GenEval results, a 7-point gain over BAGEL, and better test-time scaling than token-based generation.

entry.title: Flide: Faster Decision Inference via Exact State Forking
entry.summary: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents Flide, an inference engine that speeds up decision models used in LLM agent systems. It separates the logical tree structure of a decision request from its physical execution in a single flattened token stream, and uses ForkAttention with GPU-resident indices across standard attention and recurrent Gated DeltaNet layers. According to the authors, Flide answers queries up to 9.5 times faster than vLLM and SGLang on public hybrid and decision models, and stays closest to a float32 reference in total variation distance.

entry.title: Latent Sparse Attention: A Faster Attention Method for Ultra-Long Contexts
entry.summary: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys hierarchically in a learned latent space so queries score clusters instead of every key, reducing attention cost at ultra-long context lengths. Two variants are introduced: Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), trained only on the next-token loss. The authors report per-layer prefill and decode speedups for D-LSA at 10M tokens relative to the original sparse and full attention, and state that N-LSA matches full attention accuracy at 128k tokens with a 1.6x per-layer training speedup.

entry.title: Hierarchical World Model with Implicit Dynamics for Long-Horizon Robot Planning
entry.summary: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces ID-WM, a hierarchical world model that separates state-space reachability from low-level control. A high-level model samples feasible transitions across the state manifold, while a low-level world model acts as an inverse dynamics solver to turn these transitions into precise actions. The authors report that ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, with a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners and a 135% gain over single-level world model MPC across three navigation and manipulation suites.

entry.title: SemEllipsoid: A Method for Semantic-Aware 3D Shape Abstraction Using Ellipsoids
entry.summary: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses shape abstraction, which represents 3D shapes with a set of primitives. Prior methods focus on geometric accuracy and often let primitives span several semantic parts. The authors propose SemEllipsoid, which uses ellipsoidal primitives and injects semantic constraints from large-scale foundation models so each primitive fits a single semantic part. The method is non-learning-based, requires no network training, generalizes to arbitrary shape categories, and supports adjustable levels of abstraction.

entry.title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking via Lifted Trajectory Repair
entry.summary: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses dense 3D tracking from monocular video and presents ReLift, a feed-forward framework that treats the task as repairing and completing geometric trajectories. It starts from lifted trajectories built with pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models, and uses a trajectory corrector to fix corrupted positions and fill in motion under occlusion. The model is trained only on geometric inputs and can improve trajectories from different trackers and geometry providers without retraining. On WorldTrack, it reports state-of-the-art mean accuracy.

entry.title: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation
entry.summary: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies what the online critic in Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) needs in capacity and information to give a reliable training signal. Experiments on ImageNet across seven SiT model sizes show that enlarging the teacher while keeping the critic small can degrade students and cause collapse. The authors propose joint scaling, which grows the critic with the teacher, and a step-aware critic (STAC) that conditions on the student's generation step. Together they improve few-step distillation for ImageNet, SDXL, FLUX.2, and Wan2.1 generation.

entry.title: Exact information ledger for instance-dependent sequential limits
entry.summary: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proves instance-dependent limits for bandit regret, sequential tests, best-arm identification and Markov decision processes through one shared chain of reasoning. The authors write this chain as an exact information ledger, showing that data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence. A one-parameter family of martingale identities extends the decomposition to every tilt between two instances. The ledger is applied to seven published sources to locate where standard algorithms differ from the classical limits.

entry.title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
entry.summary: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces DecisionRank, a decision model that predicts document scores directly for reranking, avoiding autoregressive decoding. It is trained with item-space on-policy distillation, where a generative LLM teacher gives feedback on the ranked list built from the student's scores. Combined with offline ranking supervision, the authors report state-of-the-art results on TREC DL, BEIR, and BRIGHT, with substantially faster inference than the generative listwise counterpart.

entry.title: Transferability of ICU mortality prediction inputs when measurement conditions change
entry.summary: Physiological Trajectories and Observation Patterns in ICU Mortality Prediction: Transportability Under Changing Measurement Conditions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This study predicts in-hospital mortality at 48 hours for ICU patients using MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU data. It compares models built from latest-value snapshots, longitudinal physiological summaries, and measurement frequency and timing features. Physiological trajectories transferred more consistently to external data, while observation-pattern features were sensitive to the timing and availability of measurements. The authors argue that clinical prediction models should be evaluated under the measurement conditions that supply their inputs, not only in new patient populations.

entry.title: Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics
entry.summary: Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how gradient descent learns in a two-neuron ReLU teacher-student model with isotropic Gaussian inputs, trained by population gradient flow from small initialization. The authors analyze the population squared-loss landscape and show that every critical point with both student weights nonzero is either a global minimum or a saddle. They also track the gradient-flow trajectory, finding that student neurons first collapse toward a bisector saddle, then escape and specialize to the teacher neurons.

entry.title: Faster privacy loss calculation for random allocation using multiscale FFT
entry.summary: Fast Privacy Loss Accounting for Random Allocation via Multiscale FFT arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies privacy loss accounting for the random allocation sampling scheme, in which each user's data is used in k randomly chosen steps out of t. The authors introduce a multiscale FFT algorithm that reduces the running time's dependence on the accuracy parameter α from O(α^-2) to O(α^-1 log(1/α)), while keeping the accountant's guarantees. They also use a mean-preserving projection to shrink rounding errors. Experiments show speedups of several orders of magnitude at high accuracy and improved privacy bounds for DP-SGD with PREAMBLE.

entry.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer, a method for reusing context computation across models of different sizes
entry.summary: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes ACCT, a method for transferring KV cache between language models of different scales within the same model family. It converts the KV cache from a source model into sparse KV states that a target model can use directly, so the target does not need to reprocess the original context. Across five general-capability benchmarks and six context-dependent tasks, ACCT matches or exceeds the target model's original performance while cutting the KV cache size by 75%. At about 19K tokens of context, its KV conversion runs 6.5 to 21.2 times faster than target context prefill.

entry.title: SATFRONT: Machine learning method to detect weather fronts from satellite images
entry.summary: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces SATFRONT, a machine learning framework that detects cold, warm, and occluded weather fronts over Europe using geostationary satellite observations. The model is trained on frontal analyses from five European national meteorological services and evaluated against UK Met Office analyses for 2024. Using satellite data alone, it achieves a Critical Success Index of 0.428 at a 150 km tolerance, which rises to 0.591 when ERA5 reanalysis data is added.

entry.title: Enforcing exact discrete physics in a neural network for the Burgers equation via a projection layer.
entry.summary: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers) arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper extends hard constraint projection (HCP) from linear PDEs to the nonlinear one-dimensional Burgers' equation. The equation is discretised with a finite difference stencil, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) predicts velocity, which a final unlearnable layer projects onto the hyperplane of exact solutions to the discrete equation. The authors report that the HCP-PINN keeps reducing its loss after the PINN loss plateaus, reaches a data error about an order of magnitude lower on an unseen uniform grid, and is less sensitive to the choice and number of physics collocation points.

entry.title: Strategic Tanking in Stable Matching Markets: deliberately lowering one's appeal to others to improve matches
entry.summary: Strategic Tanking in Stable Matching Markets arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces strategic tanking, in which an agent intentionally makes itself less attractive to selected potential partners to improve its eventual match, without misreporting its own preferences. Cutoff tanking has exactly the same effect on the stable set as truncating one's preference list at that threshold. Arbitrary tanking can go further, producing equilibria outside the sincere stable set under proposer-deferred acceptance.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Inverse Reinforcement Learning: Modeling Rewards with Hyperbolic Distance to Infer Behavioral Goals
entry.summary: Hyperbolic Inverse Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Inverse reinforcement learning infers the reward function behind observed behavior. This paper introduces Hyperbolic IRL, which parameterizes reward as a function of hyperbolic distance between a feature vector and a learned parameter vector, along with a Euclidean distance variant. The method performs comparably to state-of-the-art models on established benchmarks under deterministic and stochastic policies, and excels in the low data limit and dense environments. Applied to human navigation among multiple museum exhibits, it reveals reward structure that depends on non-separable conjunctions between exhibit-distance features, not just individual distances.

entry.title: Effects of plasticity loss on reinforcement learning in noisy environments
entry.summary: Towards Understanding the Impact of Plasticity Loss on Reinforcement Learning in Stochastic Environments arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how loss of plasticity in neural networks affects deep reinforcement learning when environments are stochastic. The authors train SAC agents on three DeepMind Control tasks with controlled levels of observation and action noise. Plasticity-preserving methods improve robustness on the harder tasks, with the advantage growing as observation noise increases.

entry.title: CausalWAM: Learning What Causes Actions in World Action Models
entry.summary: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies world action models (WAMs), which learn latent variables from observations to both predict scene changes and generate actions. The authors note that only part of the scene causes actions, so a model may mix action-relevant variables with irrelevant ones. They prove that under a sparsity constraint, the variables used for actions are an invertible function of the action-relevant latent variables alone. They propose CWAM, which adds a sparse routing path to a pretrained WAM's action head, and experiments on synthetic data and real robots show improved closed-loop success.

entry.title: Rethinking asymmetry in self-supervised learning of 3D geometry from unposed images
entry.summary: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies self-supervised 3D geometry learning from unposed images, where models predict cameras and scene structure and render held-out views. It proposes imposing the asymmetry in the 3D representation space rather than the input space, excluding held-out views only from the reconstructed scene while a shared backbone uses all views. The authors add training signals by aligning sparse-view and dense-view features and features from a frozen vision foundation model, and report improved depth and pose estimation.

entry.title: Cost-aware stopping rule for freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization: when one-step lookahead is enough
entry.summary: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization, where candidates are trained in resumable increments and the stopping decision uses a budget-free utility of best score minus cost per increment. It analyzes a one-step expected-improvement (EI) stopping rule and constructs a certificate showing when stopping is premature, with correcting it never lowering expected utility under the surrogate. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, EI stopping is noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction helps at low costs on two of the three.

entry.title: RangeSWA: Training-free length extrapolation for continuous diffusion language models
entry.summary: RangeSWA: Training-Free Length Extrapolation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Continuous diffusion language models can suffer from repetition, semantic drift, and quality loss when generating text longer than their training length. This paper proposes RangeSWA, a training-free method that combines local sliding-window attention, remote block summaries, and dynamic content retrieval to keep local detail and access long-range context. It further reduces degradation through positional remapping, conditioning attention correction, and denoising-stage-adaptive window scheduling. Experiments on multiple continuous diffusion language models show it lowers generative perplexity and repetition rates in long-text generation.

entry.title: RAMA: Memory-Augmented Multi-Agent Routing for LEO Satellite Networks
entry.summary: RAMA: Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Agent Routing with Episodic Memory for LEO Satellite Networks arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes RAMA, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning routing framework that augments each satellite's decisions with experiences retrieved from a per-satellite episodic memory. Each satellite combines local observations, recent routing history, neighbor state, and retrieved memory entries through a Transformer-based decision network. In a 140-satellite Kepler constellation, RAMA reduces mean latency by 13.4% and 99th-percentile latency by 66.7% compared with the DDQN baseline. On the 1,584-satellite Starlink shell 1, the mean latency reduction reaches 93.2%, and online updating lowers it by a further 25.5%.

entry.title: Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Visible Evidence for AI Answers, Routing Tests, and Failed Results
entry.summary: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open specification for recording AI inferences with versioned assessments, evidence links, and explicit unknowns. It uses the SEDIM architecture from Nage AI OS as a reference implementation and reports internal experiments, including a platform-domain routing benchmark with 137 of 150 classifications correct (about 91.3%) alongside several negative or inconclusive results. The author stresses that these findings are internal and that evidence visibility does not establish correctness, causal reliance, security, or regulatory compliance.

entry.title: PersonaChatBench: Testing Chat Assistants With Varied Simulated Users
entry.summary: PersonaChatBench: Evaluating Chat Assistants with Diverse Simulated Users arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces PersonaChatBench, a framework that evaluates chat assistants by pairing the same task with multiple simulated users, each guided by a persona card describing distinct needs, preferences, and interaction behaviors. It tests 20 language models across six domains, measuring task outcomes, fulfillment of persona needs, and simulator fidelity separately. The results show that task performance and need fulfillment vary across personas and domains, and that strong task performance does not necessarily satisfy individual needs.

entry.title: CRoS: Rewarding Causal Reasoning on Scrambled Chains of Thought
entry.summary: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes CRoS, a metric for measuring whether a model's chain of thought causally affects its final answer. It scrambles the order of reasoning steps without changing their content, avoiding the confounding effects of earlier perturbation methods, and uses the metric as a training reward. On Reasoning Gym with Gemma-3-4B, CRoS reaches 46.8% accuracy on five unseen logic and game datasets versus 43.8% for the strongest baseline, and averages 43.4% CoT-Pass@K versus 41.4%. Its hint acknowledgment score is 34.0% versus 20.2% for baselines.

entry.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
entry.summary: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents REA, a unified runtime in which a deliberative high-level reasoning model, an embodied router, and fast reactive robot policies cooperate without any running policy waiting on the reasoning model. It uses a route memory of pre-measured policy success rates, a judge gate triggered at policy execution boundaries, and a shared-budget escalation ladder for recovery. On 3,000 episodes across 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks, REA reaches 95.9% success, above the best single-agent baseline (94.7%), while cutting control steps by 25% and control time by 17%.

entry.title: A Species-Level Acoustic Biodiversity Index: Classifier Benchmarks, False-Positive Control and Comparison with Standard Soundscape Indices
entry.summary: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper revises an Acoustic Biodiversity Index (ABI) built from species-level sound detections. Its main form is the Shannon diversity of detections divided by the regional species pool expected for the site and season, with temporal stability reported separately. The index was tested at an African savanna and at zoo habitats in Abu Dhabi. It correlated strongly with species richness (Spearman rho = 0.93), while six standard acoustic indices showed weaker correlations.

entry.title: Near-optimal second-order convex finite-sum optimization under individual smoothness
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies the stochastic second-order oracle complexity of smooth convex finite-sum optimization with n components. Under individual smoothness and convexity, it proves a lower bound of Ω(n+n^{5/7}ε^{-2/7}). The authors propose a Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method combined with Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration, achieving Õ(n+n^{5/7}ε^{-2/7}) complexity, which matches the lower bound up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Any Forcing: Flexible-step, stable one-step autoregressive video generation
entry.summary: Any Forcing: Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability for Autoregressive Video Generation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Any Forcing, a framework for autoregressive video generation that aims to support flexible sampling step counts while keeping one-step generation stable. A unified adversarial discriminator performs real-distribution alignment, inter-step consistency alignment, and first-frame quality enhancement. A training-free adaptive long-term memory mechanism selects historical states using global semantic relevance and local value contribution, and remaps their temporal positions. The authors report 20.9 FPS for short videos and 24.7 FPS for long videos on a single H100 GPU.

entry.title: No free loop: whether looping a trained model is worth its extra inference cost
entry.summary: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether re-applying a block of layers in an already trained model, which adds loops without adding parameters, justifies its extra cost per generated token. The authors compare looped models against an unlooped model with equal parameters and an unlooped model with equal inference FLOPs. Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B, only the looped 0.8B model beats both baselines. At 4B and 9B, the looped models do not beat the equal-parameter baseline, so adding loops after pretraining pays off only for small models with a fixed parameter budget.

entry.title: CausalXRL: Explainable reinforcement learning via causal graph reasoning
entry.summary: CausalXRL: Explainable Reinforcement Learning through Causal Graph Reasoning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces CausalXRL, a framework that uses causal graph reasoning to explain reinforcement learning agents' decisions through transparent, structured, multi-level explanations. The authors validate it with a quantitative analysis of explanation fidelity and causal-structure learning efficiency on benchmark RL environments, and a qualitative expert study on the MicroRTS real-time strategy benchmark. The results indicate faithful explanations with efficient causal-structure learning, and experts found it useful for inspecting high-level RTS strategies.

entry.title: A neural network method for estimating knot point density in real time for a nonlinear quadrotor
entry.summary: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes a learning-based method for adaptively placing knots in B-spline approximations of trajectories generated by ordinary differential equations. A neural network maps the system's initial condition to quantities describing the local variation of the trajectory. These estimates are used to build nonuniform knot distributions that roughly equalize a local error indicator, reducing the number of control points needed for a prescribed accuracy.

entry.title: Detecting When an Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty in LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression for Extrapolation
entry.summary: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper addresses uncertainty when large language models are used to discover equations from data, since many methods return only one best equation. The authors propose LLM-SR-UQ, which keeps competing equation structures and uses their disagreement to measure uncertainty about the functional form. Experiments on LLM-SRBench show the approach improves coverage under extrapolation while preserving in-distribution coverage, and it also generalizes to other symbolic-regression methods.

entry.title: Asynchronous flow map language models that build token order into one-step generation
entry.summary: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces asynchronous flow map language models (aFMLMs), which learn flow maps of asynchronous flows to incorporate prediction order into one-step parallel language modeling. The flows specify an ordering through a tokenwise time schedule that controls each token's relative denoising progress, and can use either prescribed or learned, state-adaptive schedules. The models generate all tokens in a single forward pass, and they set new state-of-the-art one-step results on Sudoku solving and code generation for GSM8K math word problems.

entry.title: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators?
entry.summary: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines why neural emulators of chaotic PDEs, trained on one-step prediction, accumulate errors when run autoregressively. A first-order decomposition separates error growth that the model's own dynamics amplify from growth that is physical and cannot be trained away, summarized as an amplification ratio. Across 21 configurations of four PDEs, five architectures and two model sizes, Jacobian fine-tuning markedly reduced error when the amplification ratio was high.

entry.title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-based turn-taking prediction for Turkish
entry.summary: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces TurnTurk-GPT, a text-based model that predicts turn-taking in Turkish conversation, built by fine-tuning a Turkish GPT-2 model on synthetic and real dialogue. It is compared with rule-based baselines, a zero-shot Turkish language model, and a multilingual end-of-turn detector on real Turkish conversation. TurnTurk-GPT outperforms the multilingual detector in both evaluation settings, but beats the zero-shot model only when test speakers appear in training. The model and evaluation protocol are publicly released.

entry.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Testing AI Negotiators on Real Trade Outcomes
entry.summary: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces TradeWar, a multi-country simulation benchmark that turns negotiation dialogue into concrete tariff and trade-share policies, applies capacity and network constraints during settlement, and scores results with an Economic Health Index. It also proposes TACTIC, an LLM agent that refines its negotiation strategy across episodes using past experience, opponent behavior, and settlement outcomes, without updating model weights. The authors report that TACTIC achieves a higher final EHI than baselines and degrades less under technology-control and energy-crisis shocks.

entry.title: GeoFlip: A Benchmark for Geometry-Sensitive Physics in Video Generation
entry.summary: GeoFlip: Benchmarking Geometry-Sensitive Physics in Video Generation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026GeoFlip is a benchmark testing whether video generation models produce correct physical outcomes when the initial scene geometry changes. It contains 482 scene pairs and 964 reference videos across six physical categories, with reference outcomes verified through physics simulation. Evaluating 16 models, the best average event correctness reached only 27.98%.

entry.title: AutoAnalysis: A Self-Updating Meta-Analysis of Human-AI Collaboration
entry.summary: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces AutoAnalysis, an automated, self-updating meta-analysis that examines when humans and AI perform better together and when they perform better alone. Its most recent run synthesizes 1,955 effect sizes from 420 papers. On average, human-AI combinations outperform humans alone but perform significantly worse than the better of humans or AI working alone. As new studies appear, the system will incorporate their findings.

entry.title: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Fixed Logit Corrections for Language Model Forgetting
entry.summary: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether the loss increase that language models suffer after instruction tuning or further pretraining on a new domain, known as forgetting, can be undone with simple fixed adjustments to final token predictions. The authors fit per-token vocabulary biases, alone or with a temperature, across 14 base and derived model pairs ranging from 1B to 7B parameters. Bias alone recovers under 10% of the loss, while bias combined with temperature recovers up to 36%, and math-pretrained models recover almost nothing.

entry.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Better Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
entry.summary: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures gate parameters of gated linear recurrences before training to improve long-context retrieval. It assigns geometric timescales across heads and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers, calibrated with a small activation sample without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI raises average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over random-initialization baselines, while language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remain broadly comparable.

entry.title: MoETok: Sparse Expert Routing for 1D Visual Tokenizers
entry.summary: MoETok: Sparse Expert Routing for 1D Visual Tokenizers arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces MoETok, a 1D visual tokenizer that routes image tokens through sparsely activated experts. The authors find that learnable queries spontaneously specialize under semantic supervision, with a small set capturing high-level content and a larger set preserving fine visual details for reconstruction. Jointly optimized with reconstruction and semantic objectives, MoETok improves reconstruction, semantic representation, and autoregressive generation over dense tokenizers under matched conditions.

entry.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Reusable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Models
entry.summary: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework for transaction risk foundation models in online payments. It encodes card, device, and account IDs with a Local Anonymous ID tokenizer that captures how each identity appears and recurs within a transaction sequence, not its specific value. A multi-scale pattern codebook is then pretrained on unlabeled sequences to turn these identity sequences into discrete behavior patterns. Experiments on an industrial dataset and six public datasets show consistent gains over strong baselines, and the method remains effective when all identity values are unseen during training.

entry.title: FoAViS: Studying learned gaze strategies in a human-like active vision system
entry.summary: FoAViS: Analyzing Learned Fixation Strategies in a Foveated Active Vision System arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents FoAViS, a machine vision system that samples input in a foveated, log-polar manner and accumulates information in a 2D spatial memory usable for both classification and segmentation. A fixation policy is trained jointly with the task to choose where to look on a 2D map. The learned policies select more informative locations than non-learned heuristics, and models trained with them outperform those trained on random locations. The resulting scanpaths partly resemble characteristics of human gaze behavior.

entry.title: TwinPast: Testing Whether Streaming Video Models Use Historical Evidence
entry.summary: TwinPast: Benchmarking Historical Evidence Use in Streaming Video Understanding with Evidence Contrastive Video Pairs arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper argues that high scores on streaming video benchmarks do not show whether models actually use visual history. It introduces TwinPast, a benchmark of 350 human-reviewed video pairs that keep recent context, question, and options fixed while changing key historical evidence and the correct answer. A model passes only if it answers correctly for both histories. Across 34 model and input configurations, the strongest streaming system reaches 49.14% PairAcc, versus 66.57-91.43% for general-purpose models.

entry.title: Gradual pruning with sparse adaptation: an efficient way to shrink large language models to extreme sparsity
entry.summary: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes ETAPS, a method for pruning weights from large language models. It tightens a global sparsity constraint in progressive stages while training a sparse delta under a small fixed budget, aiming to keep quality at high sparsity. Across six models from 125M to 13B parameters, ETAPS achieves lower perplexity than ELSA at every sparsity from 50% to 90%, with reductions of up to 42%. At 90% sparsity it also needs fewer GPUs and less persistent state and GPU-hours than ELSA.

entry.title: When is a game a Markov decision process? Links between game theory and reinforcement learning
entry.summary: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This monograph gives theorems showing that game theory and reinforcement learning describe the same objects, treating a game as a Markov decision process in three distinct senses. It covers standard game classes and solution concepts such as Nash equilibrium, the soft Bellman operator and the Shapley value, and maps each to suitable training procedures and solution complexity. It also identifies correspondences that fail, including non-stationarity for independent learners, impossibility results for uncoupled convergence to Nash equilibrium, and the gap between coarse correlated and correlated equilibria.

entry.title: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants for Boltzmann Distribution Sampling
entry.summary: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces WASABI, a method that trains a diffusion model to generate samples from a Boltzmann distribution using only the energy function. It minimizes the KL divergence between the model's distribution and the target using Wasserstein gradient flows, avoiding computation of the model's own log-density gradient. Once trained, new samples require no further energy or gradient evaluations. On alanine dipeptide, the authors report outperforming the best baselines with an estimated 3.3 times fewer energy evaluations, and competitive results on interacting particle system benchmarks.

entry.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for forecasting many related time series at once
entry.summary: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Chronos-2, a pretrained foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models interactions among multivariate time series and external covariates. It infers relationships among series from historical data and produces probabilistic forecasts without task-specific training. The authors report state-of-the-art average accuracy on various benchmarks and much faster forecast generation than specialized methods. They also show it matches or surpasses domain-specific methods in infectious-disease, macroeconomic, carbon-flux, and runoff forecasting.

entry.title: Shock loading reaches reaction pathways beyond accelerated thermolysis.
entry.summary: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper develops EMFF-MACE, a reactive machine-learning potential for C/H/N/O energetic materials, and uses it to simulate thermolysis of 20 materials and shock loading of 10 on a common potential energy surface. At matched normalized reaction progress, the two loading types show divergent chemical states and local structural environments. The authors conclude that loading history affects the structural states and subsequent reaction pathways accessed during decomposition, not just the rate of thermolysis.

entry.title: Aligning multimodal AI models with human cognition using behavior-derived semantic dimensions
entry.summary: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a framework that aligns multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with the multidimensional mental representations behind human similarity judgements. It builds on a behavior-derived semantic embedding space with 66 interpretable dimensions, derived from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out judgements. The approach improves consistency with human similarity judgements while staying competitive on standard multimodal benchmarks. Searchlight Representational Similarity Analysis on an independent fMRI dataset also shows increased representational alignment between the model and humans.

entry.title: Optimizing stochastic policy geometry for few-step flow reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Few-step flow models generate samples through a small number of large denoising steps, and applying GRPO to them requires adding randomness to those steps. This paper proposes Geo-FSRL, which selects, from a family of coefficient-preserving isotropic Gaussian transitions, the policy that minimizes conditional KL divergence, and derives a unique closed-form optimizer. The authors report higher final reward scores than Flow-GRPO and Flow-CPS on image and video generation models in the 4-step setting.

entry.title: Sensorium: An open-source library for collecting and organizing multimodal surgical data
entry.summary: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Sensorium, an open-source Python library built on ROS and ROS2 for recording, processing, annotating, and organizing multimodal data from configurable robot and sensor streams in surgery. It supports operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and generation of episodic datasets. The authors evaluated the library on 1516 recordings from phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments and report preliminary usability feedback.

entry.title: Adaptive coverage algorithms for mobile networks in dynamic environments
entry.summary: Adaptive Coverage Algorithms for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks in Dynamic Worlds arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper extends an existing framework for coordinating mobile agents in unknown spaces to handle dynamic instability. It adds two settings, Agent Loss and World Change, to the original problem. The authors improve the centralized CADENCE algorithm and its decentralized version DADENCE. On a benchmark of over 4500 test cases, the adapted algorithms outperform another state-of-the-art benchmark algorithm.

entry.title: Binary Sparse Codes: How Far Have We Come in Energy-Efficient Representations?
entry.summary: Binary Sparse Codes: Where are we on Energy Efficient Representations? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies binary sparse codes, which represent information in artificial systems using only a few active units, inspired by sparse activity in biological brains. The authors propose metrics that formalise information preservation as similarity preservation, measuring how faithfully a code reproduces the relational structure of its input. Comparing four representative methods under matched conditions, they find a trade-off between high information preservation and high sparsity. Competitive Sparse Codes is the only method reported to keep near-maximal sparsity while retaining meaningful information preservation.

entry.title: Variance reduction for decentralized optimization with multiple local updates
entry.summary: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a primal-dual decentralized optimization algorithm that combines variance reduction with multiple local updates under stochastic gradients. Its stepsize is independent of the network size and inversely proportional to the number of local updates, allowing larger stepsizes and faster convergence. In the strongly convex setting, the authors establish the first linear convergence guarantee in expectation for this setting. The method exchanges only one variable per round, halving communication cost compared with gradient-tracking methods, and numerical experiments show gains in speed and accuracy.

entry.title: IGDA-ICMH: A Framework That Adapts Features and Networks by Importance for Image Compression Serving Both Machines and Humans
entry.summary: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses image compression intended for both machine vision and human vision. The authors first quantitatively examine how different features and network layers affect machine vision task performance. Building on this, they propose the IGDA framework, which uses implicit neural representation and adds low-rank adaptation modules that adjust key network layers and exploit non-local feature properties. Experiments on image classification and object detection show better performance than existing implicit neural representation-based methods.

entry.title: How completely and cheaply retrieval methods find all the tools an LLM agent needs for multi-step requests
entry.summary: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper compares six retrieval structures for selecting tools when an LLM agent must call several of them for one request, across two multi-tool testbeds. It measures whether the top-k results contain every required tool, along with the LLM calls, tokens, and latency each method incurs. Methods that are untrained on the testbed and make at most one LLM call per query complete at most 10% of AppWorld queries at k = 16. A set-level retriever trained on in-domain queries does better with no LLM calls, while an LLM-navigated hierarchy also does better but needs many calls and about five minutes per query.

entry.title: Statistical foundations of reinforcement learning: a finite-sample analysis (monograph)
entry.summary: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This monograph systematically analyzes reinforcement learning sample complexity from a non-asymptotic perspective, based on tabular Markov decision processes. It covers three sampling settings, namely RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL, along with model-based and model-free algorithms. The emphasis is on minimax-optimal algorithm design and sharp statistical characterizations of widely used RL methods. The work also briefly discusses extensions such as robust RL, multi-agent and federated RL, uncertainty quantification, and RL from human feedback.

entry.title: ReX-GG: LLM ensemble pipeline for relation extraction and graph building
entry.summary: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents a lightweight workflow in which several large language models work together, using JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to reduce hallucinated outputs and single-model failures. The pipeline is applied to extracting four types of relations (strong causation, weak causation, contrastive, and compositional) from English popular science articles, producing interactive, colour-coded HTML causal graphs. An anonymous user study reports an average perceived accuracy of 0.778 against a human-annotated gold standard.

entry.title: Using machine learning on learners' interaction traces to measure self-efficacy in technology-enhanced learning
entry.summary: Using Machine Learning to Measure Self-Efficacy Belief Through Learners' Interaction Traces in Technology-Enhanced Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper explores whether low self-efficacy can be detected from learners' interaction traces while they solve exercises in a technology-enhanced learning system. The authors ran an experiment at two universities, collecting interaction data alongside self-reported self-efficacy measures. They built a machine learning pipeline with multiple classification models and argue that closely monitoring self-efficacy, which changes dynamically during learning, improves prediction performance.

entry.title: General AI models outperform chemistry-specific models at predicting molecular properties
entry.summary: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper compares general-purpose foundation models with chemistry-specific ones on prediction tasks across chemistry. With only 60 experimental data points, the general model GPT-6 Astra outperforms existing chemical models on five physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks. Chemical models only matched its performance with about ten times more data. The authors conclude that learning basic chemical structures does not replace training on relevant human knowledge.

entry.title: Using LLMs to automatically generate search keywords for virtual datasets
entry.summary: Automated Keyword Generation Using LLMs in a High-Volume Data Virtualization Service arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper addresses the difficulty of finding virtual datasets in a data virtualization service (DVS), where many versions of datasets are created for different tasks. The authors propose using large language models to generate keywords for each virtual dataset, and design five strategies for selecting text data to feed the models. They tested these strategies on virtual datasets from five case studies, using three LLM generators and two embedding techniques. The results show that strategy performance depends on the quality of the text descriptions, supporting a multi-strategy keyword generation service.

entry.title: Learning long-range interactions in large heterogeneous metamaterials with scientific machine learning
entry.summary: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations using field data alone. Using large-scale optical metasurfaces as a case study, the authors show full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and varying drive conditions, transfer from small to large domains, and multifunctional inverse design. The learned interactions are validated through physics-based interrogation.

entry.title: Using Question Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
entry.summary: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes TIZSKT, a method for knowledge tracing that predicts a student's next response on new platforms that have question texts but no response logs for training. It uses text as an index for building question-specific historical correctness summaries, rather than as a directly transferable representation. In leave-one-domain-out experiments on three public datasets, TIZSKT achieved the highest mean AUC and accuracy on all target domains among the evaluated baselines.

entry.title: A fuzzy model for forecasting how customer preferences change over time
entry.summary: Fuzzy selective state model for forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper forecasts how retail chain customers' preferences evolve, representing each preference as a triangular fuzzy number. The evolution is modeled by a Mamba-type selective state space model computed in a two-component fuzzy number algebra. On a synthetic example with competitor promotions and customer switching, a 107-parameter model achieves a lower forecast-centre error than two baselines and gives an interpretable estimate of forecast vagueness.

entry.title: Movens-Zero: scaling humanoid robot motion models using large-scale human videos
entry.summary: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the shortage of diverse, robot-executable data for training humanoid motion foundation models by building Movens-5M from Internet videos, containing 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid sequences. It introduces Movens-Zero, an architecture that jointly learns from text, speech, music, and video and supports real-time closed-loop execution. The authors also release Movens-Intent, a four-modality benchmark of 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs, and report consistent gains as data and model size increase.

entry.title: AI screeners favor cover letters written by certain AI models, regardless of candidate quality
entry.summary: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether the choice of large language model used to write job applications and to screen them affects hiring outcomes beyond candidate qualifications. The authors built a multi-model audit framework pairing eleven writer models with nine evaluator models across ten job descriptions and fifty candidates per job. They find a consistent global ranking of writer models, with locally hosted models disadvantaged, and evaluators showing self-preference for their own outputs. In the most adverse pairing, about 1.8 of 25 qualified candidates were filtered out solely due to model mismatch.

entry.title: Video director AI agents that learn to interact and direct together
entry.summary: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces LIT, a framework with a director agent, a simulated user, and a meta engineer that improves multistage video production and user interaction. The meta agent proactively learns external knowledge to better discover problems and propose solutions, forming a co-evolutionary closed loop with the other two components. On the Test and OOD Test splits, LIT improves production and interaction scores by 19.1% and 32.0% respectively over the initial pipeline.

entry.title: SimXAI: A Drop-in Conversational Layer Improving Dialogue Quality in Explainable AI
entry.summary: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents SimXAI, a lightweight conversational layer centered on a large language model that replaces the separate intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response modules of GUS-style explainable AI agents with a single tool-calling LLM. It also introduces an evaluation suite covering single- and multi-turn parsing, faithfulness, and contextualization. Across existing and new datasets, SimXAI achieves strong function-selection accuracy, high faithfulness, and better handling of context-dependent requests. In a user study replacing only the conversational layer of TalkToModel, users completed tasks more accurately and in fewer turns.

entry.title: Word-level and character-level similarity via path signature embeddings
entry.summary: Iterated Integrals as Lexical Fingerprints: Path Signature Embeddings for Lexical Similarity arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes building sentence embeddings from the path signatures of Word2Vec trajectories, using iterated integrals from rough path theory to capture word order and lexical structure. Ablations varying Word2Vec dimensions, signature depth, and PCA compression correlate embedding distances with five lexical string metrics. Average pooling almost entirely fails to capture character-level edit distances, while path signatures align strongly with them, with depth-2 signatures best balancing character and word-level sensitivity.

entry.title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: a hybrid model with fixed-cost memory for long sequences
entry.summary: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes the Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT), a hybrid architecture that separates sequence encoding from information reading. Its encoder uses several memory units built from dynamical systems with complex diagonal recurrent matrices, updated by an input-dependent leak rate, while its decoder uses attention to read their outputs instead of the token history. Compared with Mamba and Transformer on cognitive and language modeling tasks, DMT performs best on several cognitive tasks and comes close to Transformer on language modeling but trails Mamba. It also shows stronger length extrapolation than both on selective copy.

entry.title: Open-weight multimodal models fail to compare body parts they cannot recognize.
entry.summary: Open-Weight MLLMs Cannot Compare What They Cannot Name arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tests whether open-weight multimodal large language models can compare the size of body parts in synthetic ant images. The models fail for some body parts but not others, even though the comparison is visually simple. The authors attribute this to a recognition-driven grounding failure, where unrecognized structures are linked to recognizable semantic concepts, which impairs comparison.

entry.title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
entry.summary: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024 arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using the Capsule Vision 2024 challenge as a case study. It finds that some files are byte-identical across the public training and validation partitions, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings contributing frames appear in both. Removing Kvasir-Capsule-related training rows lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%, while the reverse comparison on other sources improves it slightly. The authors conclude the drop reflects sensitivity to source removal rather than leakage-induced inflation.

entry.title: ObjectGuidedMap: An object-aware model for reliable bird's-eye-view map prediction under heavy occlusion
entry.summary: ObjectGuidedMap: An Object-Aware Model for Robust Bird's Eye View Map Prediction in High-Occlusion Scenarios arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a multitask architecture that jointly predicts bird's-eye-view (BEV) maps and 3D objects so the two tasks can share information. Building on Mask2Map, it adds an object detection branch and fuses features across tasks at both the BEV feature and instance-query levels using deformable and cross-attention. Experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 show improved map prediction accuracy, with a 21% mAP gain in scenes with heavy object occlusion.

entry.title: Feed-forward camera localization using simple planar map primitives instead of complex maps (PGGT-Loc)
entry.summary: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes localizing cameras by matching a query image directly to compact map primitives, such as planes, rather than to costly dedicated maps. The authors implement this idea as PGGT, a Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer that takes one query image and a set of planar primitives and predicts a 6-DoF camera pose in a single feed-forward pass. The method is said to generalize to unseen environments. The authors report improved localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models, and the code and models are publicly available.

entry.title: Trainable vector quantization for compressing large language models
entry.summary: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes TVQ, a method for compressing large language model weights with vector quantization to reduce memory use and speed up inference. It uses straight-through estimation so that vector-quantized models can be optimized with gradient descent, applied within a block-wise knowledge distillation framework. In experiments, TVQ reaches state-of-the-art quality in low-bit post-training quantization, achieving near-lossless 2-bit quantization for LLaMA2-70B with only a 1% accuracy drop on popular question-answering benchmarks.

entry.title: ElTab: An elastic looped tabular transformer that adapts to different compute budgets
entry.summary: ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Tabular transformers such as TabPFN predict well but are costly at inference, which makes deployment in resource-limited settings hard. The authors propose the Elastically Looped Tabular Transformer (ElTab), a single model trained with supervision at randomly sampled early exits so it can run under different computational budgets. Across 30 OpenML classification datasets, one ElTab model matches six depth-specific looped models while cutting training cost by more than half, and matches a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs.

entry.title: DIFFNAS: Predictor-free neural architecture search using diffusion models and zero-cost evaluation
entry.summary: DIFFNAS: Predictor-Free Neural Architecture Search via Diffusion Model and Zero-Cost Evaluation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026DIFFNAS is a neural architecture search method that does not need a performance predictor. It uses a discrete graph diffusion model guided by training-free metrics such as MeCo and SWAP. On NAS-Bench-201 it finds optimal architectures for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 while cutting search cost by up to 17.5x compared with DiffusionNAG, but its accuracy on the MobileNetV3 search space is lower than DiffusionNAG's.

entry.title: RECAST: Rebuilding Chain-of-Thought Reasoning from Auditable Structured Traces
entry.summary: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Closed-source reasoning models usually reveal only final answers, hiding the intermediate reasoning. Existing chain-of-thought extraction methods rely on side channels such as visible reasoning fields, but the authors found that three such methods returned no reasoning tokens from Claude-Sonnet-5.5 via a standard chat interface. RECAST reconstructs a first-person structured rationale from the question and the model's final answer, producing data ready for supervised fine-tuning. The system is open-source and packaged as an agent skill.

entry.title: Continual RL as an Integration Problem: Ten Design Desiderata
entry.summary: Continual Reinforcement Learning Is an Integration Problem arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes ten opinionated desiderata for designing and evaluating reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually over a lifetime. The authors use them to review representative existing approaches and argue that all ten should ultimately be integrated within a single agent. They also present a compact persistent-world scenario as a companion and outline a benchmark that tests related behavioral capabilities together within one lifetime.

entry.title: Training Time-Series Classifiers Without Backpropagation
entry.summary: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper adapts three backpropagation-free learning rules (DFA, DRTP, and NoProp) to 1D convolutional networks and systematically compares them on 112 datasets from the UCR time series archive. The optimized methods reach mean F1 scores of 0.76 to 0.79, below ROCKET (0.83) and InceptionTime (0.84). Intra-class temporal variability is the dataset property most consistently linked to the performance gap, and the study reports computational costs relative to backpropagation.

entry.title: Pre-training to Estimate Uncertainty for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials Beyond Training Data
entry.summary: Towards Out-of-Distribution Uncertainty Quantification for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials via Pre-Training arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes pre-training uncertainty estimators for machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) on large, diverse materials science datasets to broaden their applicability. The authors pre-train several uncertainty models and evaluate them on in-distribution and out-of-domain adsorption-energy predictions. Pre-trained estimators give viable zero-shot uncertainty estimates across multiple datasets, and fine-tuning yields positive correlations between predicted uncertainty and prediction error, even on the most challenging datasets.

entry.title: Detecting body-blocked signals on chest-worn UWB tags using machine learning or link indicators
entry.summary: On-device Detection of Wearer-induced NLOS on Chest-worn UWB Tags: Machine Learning, Link Indicators, or Both? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how to detect non-line-of-sight conditions caused by a wearer's body on ultra-wideband (UWB) tags worn on the chest. The authors evaluate 21 existing on-device machine learning and link-indicator classifiers and propose new hybrid methods that combine their strengths. Results on 1.5 million samples show that accuracy, ranging error, and energy use vary widely with channel and PHY settings. A recommender tool for selecting classifiers under user-defined constraints is also released.

entry.title: Accurate, auditable ECG classification using visibility graph neural networks
entry.summary: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. It reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889 on CODE-Test, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while using about 14% of the storage of full-sample graphs. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, deleting clinically defined waveform regions and altering beat timing lets the authors audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions.

entry.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Re3Culture for Grounding Cultural Value Alignment
entry.summary: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset that grounds cultural value alignment in real human evidence, drawing on 700+ participants across four cultures. It links community-selected culturally sensitive scenarios with value surveys, behavioral principles, and explicit value priorities. The authors find that estimating cultural values requires both community affiliation and broad internal coverage, that values should be observed in concrete situations, and that value priorities should be elicited explicitly rather than inferred from response preferences.

entry.title: Unstated Task Assumptions in Continual Learning
entry.summary: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper argues that continual learning research usually splits data into sequential tasks without clearly stating whether properties such as task similarity, the rate of data change and presentation order belong to the underlying data, the task partition, or the learner. Controlled teacher-student experiments show that partitioning the same data trajectory at different granularities, changing the presentation order, or varying the similarity structure of the data each produce different measured outcomes. The authors also review representative benchmarks to see which of these properties are stated.

entry.title: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Pretrained-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation
entry.summary: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CoFailMed, an audit that checks whether pretrained encoder pools fail on the same cases in medical image segmentation. Across five 2D tasks, it evaluates 11 public encoders using frozen features and separately trained readouts. Models sharing a checkpoint show the highest per-case Dice correlation, and checkpoints within the same encoder family remain more correlated than cross-family pairs. The authors argue that pool evaluation should report absolute dependence and threshold-specific effective size alongside accuracy and nominal pool size.

entry.title: Face recognition method that decorrelates attention heads more strongly for hard samples
entry.summary: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes ViT-HarDis, which makes attention head decorrelation in Vision Transformers depend on sample difficulty. Hard samples with high cosine similarity to negative class centers receive stronger decorrelation so that heads specialize where identity ambiguity is highest. The method improves on the baseline and uniform decorrelation on most benchmarks without architectural changes or added inference cost.

entry.title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Hierarchical Structure from Retrieval Embeddings
entry.summary: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper finds that in Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) embeddings, the length of leading prefixes aligns with the coarse-to-fine granularity of gold taxonomies. It introduces PEEL, a minimal probe trained on frozen embeddings with an order-embedding objective, and decodes taxonomic DAGs using a minimum spanning arborescence. Using only a concept vocabulary, PEEL achieves high structural fidelity on two OLLM benchmarks and transfers to a new domain without target-edge supervision.
